Blackpool set sights on League Two boss as potential Ian Evatt replacement

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (550 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that blackpool sacked Ian Evatt last week, leaving the Tangerines on the lookout for a new boss.
  • According to recent reports, now, a newly introduced name has been linked with the vacancy at Bloomfield Road.
  • Lawlor has drawn high praise for his work with the Seasiders’ North West coast neighbours, where he has been in permanent charge since March.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that blackpool sacked Ian Evatt last week, leaving the Tangerines on the lookout for a new boss. They were defeated in their first game under Steve Thompson’s interim lead, losing to fellow strugglers Wigan Athletic 2-1 at home.

According to recent reports, now, a newly introduced name has been linked with the vacancy at Bloomfield Road. According to reporter Pete O’Rourke, one man under consideration for the job at Blackpool is Fleetwood Town boss Matt Lawlor.

Lawlor has drawn high praise for his work with the Seasiders’ North West coast neighbours, where he has been in permanent charge since March. The 38-year-old is under contract with Fleetwood until the summer of 2028 at present, so a compensation fee would be required to bring him in as Evatt’s replacement.

Industry observers note that born in Poulton-le-Fylde, Lawlor is a North West native. He played for Blackpool’s youth academy as a youngster before going on to play non-league football with Farsley Celtic, AFC Fylde and Bamber Bridge.

Sources indicate that he coached alongside his playing career from a young age, working with Manchester United before joining the Fleetwood Town setup in 2019. Lawlor held various roles in their academy and spent a few spells at their sister club Waterford FC, serving as assistant manager once and caretaker boss twice.

An impressive stint as temporary boss of the Cod Army in January 2026 saw Lawlor given his maiden full-time gig in senior football, and he has made a good impression. He isn’t blessed with resources at Highbury Stadium, but he’s delivered respectable results through fine match preparation and some smart in-game coaching, as shown by the shock Carabao Cup win over Premier League champions Arsenal.

Lawlor’s future at Fleetwood is secure with a contract until 2028, but that might not be enough to fend off interest from elsewhere.

Sources indicate that lawlor’s good work at Fleetwood Town means interest from Blackpool is more than justified. It could prove a tempting opportunity too.

Industry observers note that geographically, he could make the step up to League One without having to move away from home. His past as a youth player at Bloomfield Road could mean there are sentimental temptations as well.

That mentioned, it does feel as though Lawlor is in a good place right now. After various roles in the Fishermen’s setup and at Waterford, he has developed well. He’s still only 38 and in the formative years of his time as a first-team boss too, so may be wary of making the step up too early.

Time will tell whether the rumoured interest comes to anything, with Blackpool sure to be considering plenty of contenders.

Blackpool sack their manager just seven hours after wishing him happy birthday: 'Have a great day, Gaffer!'

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 15:24 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 16:32 EST, 19 November 2026.
  • Blackpool have sacked manager Ian Evatt just hours after wishing him a happy birthday.
  • According to recent reports, evatt had been in charge for a year and his final match was Saturday's 1-0 away defeat by fellow strugglers AFC Wimbledon, when his squad was decimated by illness.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 15:24 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 16:32 EST, 19 November 2026.

Blackpool have sacked manager Ian Evatt just hours after wishing him a happy birthday.

According to recent reports, evatt had been in charge for a year and his final match was Saturday's 1-0 away defeat by fellow strugglers AFC Wimbledon, when his squad was decimated by illness. The result left the Seasiders immediately above the League One relegation zone and followed a run of one win and six defeats in ten league games.

Blackpool’s social media team had earlier wished Evatt a happy 45th birthday with the pay-off line: 'Have a great day, Gaffer!'.

Three hours later, Evatt was relieved of his duties, and the club began the search for their ninth manager in eight years.

Recent findings suggest that evatt’s contract was set to run until June 2028. He joined last October following his exit from Bolton Wanderers in January 2025.

Blackpool later thanked the 45-year-old for his efforts during his time with the club.

Blackpool sacked manager Ian Evatt just hours after wishing him a happy 45th birthday.

Blackpool posted the birthday message just after 9am in the morning, with Evatt's sacking then confirmed at 4pm.

Former Crystal Palace chairman Simon Jordan famously claimed to have sacked Trevor Francis on his birthday back in 2003.

Francis' dismissal has become an often told tale, with Jordan writing sixteen years after the event that he had even offered to send the former England star a birthday card.

Recent reports have also involved the suggestion that Francis had mumbled 'but its my birthday' back to Jordan when he was given his marching orders.

It has been revealed that whether these events played out as told are unclear. But Crystal Palace officially confirmed Francis' departure on April 18 in 2003, with his birthday falling a day later.

Sources indicate that 'I am totally committed to playing in the Premier League and I will ensure the fresh manager can achieve this aspiration,' Jordan wrote on Crystal Palace's website at the time. 'I would like to thank Trevor for all his hard work and would like to wish him the very best for the future.'.

Jordan then turned on the players, adding: 'I'm not watching next year what I've had to watch this year. At times we've been a disgrace.

It has been revealed that 'I've asked the management staff to tell me who should go. They can see the players who are performing and those who are not and you will see in the summer, out they will go. The players will be told when it suits me. I care about them as much they care about me.'.

Francis had reportedly told his players in a parting shot: 'Well, lads, I've been sacked – have a good summer holiday.'.

Palace appointed Steve Kember as manager in the summer and despite Jordan's hopes of automatic promotion, rather than the play-offs, found themselves in a relegation battle in November.

Iain Dowie was appointed as manager the following month and guided Palace into the play-offs, with the Eagles triumphing in Cardiff to secure promotion to the top flight.

Steve Thompson will step in to take charge of the team against Wigan Athletic this weekend, his fourth spell as caretaker, alongside Stephen Crainey, Stephen Dobbie and Steve Banks.

It has been revealed that during a hugely successful playing career at Bloomfield Road, Evatt made over 250 appearances for Blackpool. In his six years at the club, he played a vital role in their rise from League One to the Premier League, which included two successful play-off campaigns.

On arrival as a manager, he amassed 13 points from a possible 15 in December 2025 to lift them out of the relegation zone, although they lost ten and won two of their next 15 matches in all competitions.

They finished the campaign strongly, with six wins in seven games as part of a sequence of one defeat in 13 between mid-March and the end of August, only to struggle again this season.

Breaking: £3m Southampton man must seek St Mary’s exit in January after Tonda Eckert decision

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (982 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Southampton returned to winning ways with a convincing 2-0 win over Derby County on Saturday, but one selection decision made by Tonda Eckert will have one player really questioning his role in the Saints squad.
  • One of the main contributors to Southampton's strong start this season has been their injury bill, which has, for the most part, been impeccable.
  • That's left some fringe players without the minutes they'd ideally want, but on Saturday, there was a big chance for Mads Roerslev to finally stake a claim for some starts in the future, as James Bree was sidelined with a minor injury.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Southampton returned to winning ways with a convincing 2-0 win over Derby County on Saturday, but one selection decision made by Tonda Eckert will have one player really questioning his role in the Saints squad.

One of the main contributors to Southampton's strong start this season has been their injury bill, which has, for the most part, been impeccable.

That's left some fringe players without the minutes they'd ideally want, but on Saturday, there was a big chance for Mads Roerslev to finally stake a claim for some starts in the future, as James Bree was sidelined with a minor injury.

However, the Dane was once again left on the bench, despite being the only fit recognised right-back in Tonda Eckert's squad. Even if he still managed to get his first league minutes of the season off the bench, the writing is surely on the wall regarding the former Brentford man's status in this Saints side.

Industry observers note that roerslev was an intriguing signing for Southampton last season. Arriving from Brentford for £3 million, he went under the radar in a window that also saw big-money feespaid for the likes of Finn Azaz, Casper Jander, Tom Fellows and Leo Scienza.

In a recent development, at Brentford, though, the Dane was a useful squad player in their rise to the Premier League and the years that followed under Thomas Frank. He started every game of their successful play-off run in 2021, and in the 2023/24 campaign, he played in all but four Premier League games.

Unfortunately, Roerslev's time at Southampton so far has been largely associated with how terrible the Saints were under Will Still at the start of last season. All of the 27-year-old's starts at St Mary's came under the Belgian.

When Still was sacked in early November last year, it presented a good opportunity for the squad to impress under new, young, exciting interim coach Tonda Eckert, but Roerslev was almost immediately sidelined.

He played in Eckert's first two games, wins against QPR and Sheffield Wednesday, before going down with an Achilles injury, which would see him out for the rest of the season.

Recent findings suggest that roerslev had to watch on from the sidelines as Southampton were rampant in the second half of the season under Eckert. The Saints didn't lose a league game from January 17th until the end of the campaign, and made the FA Cup semi-finals, too.

During that time, James Bree became an unlikely hero at St Mary's, coming back from his loan spell at Charlton Athletic in January and immediately being thrown back into Saints contention under Eckert.

The 28-year-old went into this season as the first choice at right-back, but a returning Roerslev from injury made for a good backup in theory, keeping with the theme at Southampton currently that there are two top players in each position.

In practice, that hasn't been the case with Bree out, though, as the former one-time Danish international has remained on the fringes, even when the position has been open.

Recent findings suggest that against Norwich City last month, Bree was rested after playing every minute of the first nine league games of the season. In his place, though, came natural centre-back, Zach Abbott, who has also been a victim of the pecking order so far this season.

With Abbott coming in to play in the middle of the back four against Derby on Saturday and with Bree out injured, though, it gave Roerslev a significant chance for his first start in over a year. But in came natural midfielder Flynn Downes, with the Dane having to settle for a nine-minute cameo.

Do you think Mads Roerslev deserves more game time at Southampton? Let us know in the comments.

Those were his first minutes of the season, but they don't indicate a resurgence in the squad.

In a way, the decisions that Tonda Eckert made regarding formation in his first few months at the helm at St Mary's have foreshadowed Roerslev's position in the pecking order right now.

Southampton flip-flopped between a back three and a back four during Will Still's uneventful few months in charge. One of the first things Eckert did was stick with a back three, but Roerslev wasn't his first choice off the right.

In a recent development, indeed, in the German's first two games in charge, the two games Roerslev was fit and available for, Tom Fellows was preferred at right wing back. Saints looked to attack more down the right, and the former West Brom man was selected ahead of a natural right-back.

Then, when Bree returned from his loan spell at Charlton, that was when Eckert moved to a flat back four, which he has used almost exclusively since; the one exception being against Manchester City in the FA Cup semi-final.

Industry observers note that perhaps then, Roerslev's place in the pecking order was clear from the off. Eckert didn't favour him over a winger in a small sample size last season, so trusting Downes to play there against Derby may not be much of a surprise.

Football's a squad game, and Southampton may prefer to have someone with the experience of Roerslev in their reserves in case they encounter injuries during the second half of the season.

However, it's becoming apparent that the 27-year-old needs a fresh change of scenery to try and kickstart his career once more.

Industry observers note that just three seasons ago, Roerslev was a regular player in a Premier League squad, making the Danish national team and not looking out of place within it. He has the quality, but isn't able to showcase it in Southampton's reserves.

Tonda Eckert has shown that he's comfortable playing central defenders or midfielders out of position at right-back, so letting him go to start afresh in January shouldn't detriment them, either.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has claimed that it is 'not the right moment' to be talking about a latest contract at Old Trafford.
  • Fernandes will lead out the Red Devils against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday afternoon, with Mauricio Pochettino looking to mark his arrival at Old Trafford with a statement win.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 22 Nov 2026 12:16.

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has claimed that it is 'not the right moment' to be talking about a latest contract at Old Trafford.

Fernandes will lead out the Red Devils against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday afternoon, with Mauricio Pochettino looking to mark his arrival at Old Trafford with a statement win.

Pochettino has confirmed that the Portuguese will remain as skipper, but reports emerged earlier this week that the playmaker is yet to accept an offer of a upcoming deal.

Should Fernandes pen fresh terms at a time when Man United sit in the relegation zone of the Premier League table, it would represent a major boost for the club.

However, speaking in an interview with Sky Sports, Fernandes has suggested that he has no intention of committing his future to United anytime soon.

While Fernandes spoke positively over club officials making an attempt to extend his contract, he is keen to focus on matters on the pitch.

The former Sporting Lisbon star said: "The club offered me a fresh contract, so I think that, from their side, indicates that they want me to stay.

"There's no negotiations ongoing, but I've seen people saying that 'he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years'. If I wanted more money, I wouldn't be here.

"I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester.

"Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here.".

He added: "We spoke about the contract at the end of last season.

"We came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations.

"The most crucial thing now is that the club gets back to winning games.".

Unless Man United move clear of the Premier League relegation zone, it is highly unlikely that Fernandes will be signing a new contract.

That would make no sense for either party, regardless of Fernandes said to have admirers in AC Milan, who are managed by former United boss Ruben Amorim.

United can activate a 12-month option to protect their position, and that feels like the most realistic development over the coming months.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, west Ham United's stop-start 2026-27 season continued on Saturday with a 1-1 draw at home to Preston North End which saw them drop to tenth place in the Championship while leaving fresh manager Scott Parker still chasing his first win since replacing at the start of November.
  • Recent findings suggest that successes at The London Stadium have been thin on the ground this season, but one of the players that has shone for them so far has been Arne Engels.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arne Engels is of interest to Stuttgart, even though Celtic only sold the midfielder to West Ham United in the summer, and this could mean a windfall for the Scottish giants.

According to recent reports, west Ham United's stop-start 2026-27 season continued on Saturday with a 1-1 draw at home to Preston North End which saw them drop to tenth place in the Championship while leaving fresh manager Scott Parker still chasing his first win since replacing at the start of November. The Irons are now three points adrift of a play-off position, and they're now five consecutive games without a League win.

Recent findings suggest that successes at The London Stadium have been thin on the ground this season, but one of the players that has shone for them so far has been Arne Engels. The Belgian midfielder signed for the club from Celtic in the summer for £22 million, but such has been the calibre of his performances that he's already starting to draw attention from other clubs despite only having signed a five-year contract with West Ham in August.

The Glasgow Times have reported on Monday morning that Arne Engels stay at West Ham United could turn out to be a brief one. They report that the midfielder is of interest to the Bundesliga club Stuttgart amid speculation that one of their midfielders, Angelo Stiller, could be on his way out of the club.

But Engels isn't the only midfielder who could be of interest to Stuttgart as a replacement for Stille, with the Glasgow Times also reporting that the German club could be interested in Caspar Jander of Southampton and Aidan Morris of Middlesbrough.

It has been revealed that how much do you think West Ham should seek, if they're to sell Arne Engels on? Let us know in the comments below!

They report that "Celtic are likely to have included a sell-on percentage in the deal and could be set to benefit from any future move", though there is no clarification of what that percentage might be, while it hasn't been confirmed that such a clause actually exists.

In a recent development, and they also report that the price could become something of a sticking point, given that West Ham paid a Championship-record £22 million for him in the summer, and signed him on a five-year contract. This situation puts the East London club firmly in control of the player's future, and may well push his price above what Stuttgart are prepared to pay for him.

The news that Arne Engels is of interest to Stuttgart has provoked considerable comment on social media, so here's a selection of what's being said about it.

This West Ham fan believes that Engels could be leaving the club at exactly the right time:.

And this fan doesn't feel that West Ham have seen enough from Engels, considering the amount of money they paid for him:.

This fan feels that Engels' signing was indicative of a broader problem with his club's recruitment policies in recent seasons:.

And this fan has a fee that he feels any buyer should be paying for the player:.

There are clearly disgruntled West Ham United fans whose patience with Arne Engels has already run out, but their exasperation isn't quite borne out by the statistics for him. Fotmob match ratings for the midfielder demonstrate a succession of decent performances this season from the player, even though West Ham's team performances have not delivered the results that supporters would have been hoping for.

But even in the event that Engels were to leave West Ham, it's doubtful that he would be able to play for Stuttgart this season. FIFA rules explicitly state that, while players can be registered to play for three different clubs over a 12-month period, they can only play for two of them, and as Engels' sale to West Ham only went through in the middle of August, by which time he'd already played in two SPFL games for Celtic, he would ordinarily be prevented from playing for Stuttgart as well, though there are exceptions to this rule for clubs who play to different calendars.

Recent findings suggest that the Glasgow Times' reporting confirms that the speculation over Angelo Stiller concerns a potential move next summer, meaning that West Ham would retain his services for the remainder of 2026-27. This would at least mean that they don't have to scramble for a replacement for him themselves during the January transfer window. Whether the news of potential Bundesliga interest in him is connected to another recent announcement, that Engels has changed his agent, is not known.

West Ham United's performances so far throughout 2026-27 have not matched pre-season expectations, so it's unsurprising that fans are turning their ire on their underperforming players. But having already been capped four times by the Belgian national team, it's clear that there is talent in Arne Engels, and perhaps the best way to get the best out of him would be to get back up into the promotion hunt and secure a quick return to the Premier League. Recent results have not shown much indication that this is going to happen, but the possibility of Premier League football in 2027-28 could yet prevent the player's head from being turned by the possibility of a move to Germany.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Swansea City and Burnley are in contrasting positions in the Championship table, with the Swans still inside the play-offs and the Clarets stuck in the relegation zone. While both look to rediscover form on the pitch though, work is going on to identify potential targets for the January transfer window.

Now, a report from Football League World has claimed that the Championship pair are both interested in Huddersfield Town hotshot Joe Taylor. It is said that they are ‘weighing up’ moves for the 24-year-old striker as the next window approaches.

Taylor has been in excellent form this season with 12 goals and three assists in 18 games across all competitions. He is currently under contract until the summer of 2029; that and his form means it will take a handsome fee to prise him away from the Terriers this winter.

Despite his age and the fact he has moved around clubs a fair amount, Taylor is an established name in the EFL with 143 appearances to his bame across the Championship, League One and League Two.

Sources indicate that peterborough United signed him from non-league side Kings Lynn Town, and Luton Town bought him from there. Taylor impressed in loans with Colchester United (27 games, 12 goals, two assists) and Lincoln City (19 games, 10 goals, three assists) but failed to score in 19 outings for the Hatters.

Strong loan form prompted Huddersfield Town to snap him up, and Taylor’s Terriers career has come to life after another successful temporary move, this time to Wigan Athletic (22 games, 11 goals). The Welshman has proven to be a prolific scorer in League One and he is starring at the level once again, scoring for fun in Martin Drury’s attack alongside fellow star Derensili Sanches Fernandes.

Given his success in League One, it feels inevitable that Taylor gets another shot in the Championship. Swansea City and Burnley could offer him such a chance, but they will have to pay a good fee for his services.

Of the two interested clubs, Swansea City are no doubt the more attractive option at the moment. Despite the fact they are presently managerless, the Swans are in the hunt for a Championship play-off finish, and with the help of Jamestown Analytics, they are capable of making some long-awaited strides forward.

But, for Taylor, a move to Burnley may be better. Swansea have all of Zan Vipotnik, Adam Idah and Ross Stewart on the books for their one-striker system, so they do not need another.

Sources indicate that as for the Clarets, they have plenty of strikers, but none are impressing. He would quickly jump up the pecking order and into contention for a starting spot against Jamie Vardy, Andreas Hountondji and Zeki Amdouni, and on current form, he’d be backed to beat them.

Alternatively though, a stay at Huddersfield Town could be best. The Terriers will have little interest in selling someone key to their promotion push, and he could end up in the Championship in their colours sooner rather than later.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Perhaps the only thing more English in terms of culture than football and the EFL is the pub – and the two things go hand in hand.

The erosion of working-class culture when it comes to English football is something that perhaps requires more discussion and that, again, goes hand in hand with the almost relentless closing down of pubs up and down the country.

Despite that, plenty remain standing, albeit perhaps less than there once was when clubs were a bit more ramshackle in the heart of a community, rather than often moved out to industrial estates.

That stated, we have taken a look at the Championship and ranked the clubs with the most pubs within two miles of the ground.

Having moved away from the town centre in the late-1990s, there are still a few pubs inside a two-mile radius of Bolton Wanderers’ home, albeit most of the locals tend to go further afield into Horwich or even via the train from town. The Beehive is the designated away fans’ pub.

The Railway Inn is just 0.2 miles away from Swansea City’s home ground of the Swansea.com Stadium but there aren’t really an abundance of other options with just 15 pubs within a two-mile radius of The Jacks’ home ground in Wales’ second city.

In a recent development, with some nearby pubs such as The Royal Consort and The White Hart, there are 16 pubs within a two-mile radius of Deepdale. Preston North End supporters are blessed with quite a few more options in what is often a lively and entertaining city centre, though.

It has been revealed that not too far from the city centre, it is somewhat surprising that there is a slight shortage of pubs within two miles of Lincoln City’s home ground of Sincil Bank. There are around 18 with the closest being Lincoln’s home pub, The Imp and Angel, just 0.2 miles from the ground.

There are a few extremely busy pubs nearby to the Riverside Stadium, perhaps most prominently The Navigation, but there aren’t an abundance of options with around 20 pubs inside a two-mile limit of Middlesbrough’s home ground.

Carrow Road has 20 pubs within a two-mile radius of the ground with Norwich City supporters having plenty of options within half a mile, too, such as the Coach and Horses, The Fat Cat and Canary as well as The Jubilee.

With The Turf more or less attached to the Racecourse Ground, that tends to be the haunt for Wrexham supporters but The Red Dragons do have 20 pubs within the two mile cut off in North Wales.

Recent findings suggest that up in the heart of Lancashire, there are still plenty of pubs knocking about and there are 21 pubs within a two-mile radius of Ewood Park. The Fox and Hounds and The Fernhurst are the closest on a Blackburn Rovers match day.

Slightly out of the centre, there are still around 22 pubs in close proximity of Pride Park for Derby County supporters with the closest and most popular being The Merlin, 0.3 miles away from the ground.

Sources indicate that down in Bermondsey, there are around 25 pubs within two miles of Millwall’s famous home ground of The Den. It is often the case that away supporters head into Central London and around the London Bridge area before the short tube down to The Lions.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 18:03 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 18:07 EST, 19 November 2026.

As far as auditions to replace Cristiano Ronaldo go, Carlos Forbs' couldn't have gone much better.

His winner against Wales on Tuesday certainly looked and felt like a Ronaldo goal, especially from early in the former Manchester United star's career.

Right flank. Dribbling at pace. Ben Davies back-tracking. A quick flap inside with the left boot. Shoot. Goal. He only needed 11 minutes since coming on to change the game - and potentially his career trajectory.

According to recent reports, portugal's No7 later insisted he did not feel the 'weight' of the shirt, but the jersey is pregnant with meaning. Ronaldo wore No 7 for the national team for 20 years, inheriting it from the legendary Luis Figo. Its next permanent incumbent matters deeply in the Portuguese footballing psyche.

Sources indicate that forbs has not inherited it full-time yet, as a source within the Portugal camp has confirmed to Daily Mail Sport. He appears locked in a battle with Rafael Leao, who was supposed to have it this international break until he missed out through injury.

But now Forbs - a chap who went to school in Leeds and was praised by Erling Haaland while at Manchester City - is the name on fans' lips.

Carlos Forbs is gunning to be Portugal's latest full-time No7 after Cristiano Ronaldo's retirement - and his audition against Wales went swimmingly.

Ronaldo held the shirt for 20 years, having inherited it from the legendary Luis Figo.

They are already calling him 'CF7' and media outlets across the world hailed the 22-year-old, a relative unknown for plays for Club Brugge. 'The latest national hero,' is how leading Portuguese outlet O Jogo described him. No pressure, kid.

His form is attracting attention on British shores. Rangers were interested in him over the summer, as were Lyon. Daily Mail Sport has been unable to verify recent reports that the likes of Arsenal, Aston Villa, Everton and Newcastle are keen.

It has been revealed that but it would be no surprise to see him in the Premier League one day. Stardom has long felt like it might be on the cards for Forbs. Born in Sintra to Bissau-Guinean parents, he started off playing futsal and was picked up by Sporting Lisbon's academy, just like Ronaldo. His family left for England when he was just 11, and it wasn't long before Manchester City came calling.

The attacker spent eight years in the City academy and was considered a gem. In 2022-23 he was named Premier League 2 player of the season after a stunning campaign which saw him score 29 goals and provide 18 assists in all competitions.

He had a knack of scoring hat-tricks - not a bad habit to adopt. In one match he scored four against Manchester United like it was child's play. It felt like nothing could go wrong for the winger, who copied Ronaldo's lesser-known 'nap' celebration to mock the Red Devils. A player who looked up to the likes of Raheem Sterling and Phil Foden didn't look far off joining them in the first team.

In a recent development, he was rewarded with chances to train alongside Pep Guardiola's seniors, and Kyle Walker and Bernardo Silva were noted as being particularly welcoming. Erling Haaland was impressed with him. Watching a montage including the youngster's goals, he mentioned: 'Is that Carlos? I've been training a lot with these guys. Carlos is good.'.

But a debut never came due to the competition at City and in 2023, yearning for opportunities to play in the major-time, he moved to Ajax in a £17million deal.

'I didn’t have to leave, but in the summer, clubs came along where I knew I had more prospects,' he told AD in October 2023, while he was still known as Carlos Borges.

Forbs, previously known as Carlos Borges, was a gem in Manchester City's academy but never got a first-team debut.

He was shipped off to Ajax but struggled to nail down a starter spot and was harshly cast aside.

Sources indicate that 'The media made me big, but I didn’t really feel like I was getting many opportunities in Manchester. I didn’t know if that would change this season. Of course, I already knew that Ajax focuses on youth. When I heard the looks, I thought OK, I want to try my luck at this club.

It has been revealed that 'A number of staff members at Manchester City also wanted to see me make the final step after ten years. Me too, at the club where I grew up, just as it was my parents’ dream. But I concluded that it was even better to take this opportunity.'.

But things didn't work out for Forbs in the Netherlands. Playing for such a dominant side against low blocks did not suit his electric pace and direct dribbling, even though he had managed at Manchester City, who had a similar philosophy.

He was a bit-part player in his first season and, in his second, was sent on loan to Wolves, where he had little impact in 10 Premier League appearances. While he had more game time under Gary O'Neil, he did not fit into Vitor Pereira's 3-4-2-1 system, which favoured wing-backs, when the Portuguese replaced the Englishman.

Recent findings suggest that by the summer of 2025, Ajax had seen enough, and dispensed of Forbs in brutal fashion. Technical director Alex Kroes informed seven players, including him, over WhatsApp that he was 'no longer welcome' at the club's training ground. Former Arsenal man Chuba Akpom was among them, too.

If Forbs wanted to train, he had to wait until the first team were done. Even if it was a day of double sessions, he had to stay away until both were over. With three years remaining on his contract, his space in the car park had reportedly been removed. Access to the gym and canteen was only permitted when the first team were finished.

A once-dream move had soured within two years and he was cast away savagely, joining Belgian side Club Brugge - and that is where his career has been reborn.

Early into his Brugge career, in November 2025, he announced himself in Europe by scoring two goals and providing an assist against Barcelona in the Champions League.

Forbs has shone for Club Brugge and scored twice against Barcelona last season.

'Today is a dream come true,' he remarked after being awarded man of the match against Barca. It was the sort of night his youth coaches had known he was capable of.

Sources indicate that after 10 goals in all competitions last season, he is already on five for this campaign and growing his reputation. He is on three Portugal caps now - he made his debut last year - and seems to have the trust of newly introduced manager Jorge Jesus.

Sources indicate that when pressed if he was the newly introduced permanent Portugal No7 on Tuesday, Forbs was coy. 'I try to do my best,' he mentioned.

Then he added: 'We know it's a massive, blessed number and I hope to continue wearing this number and scoring many goals.'.

It remains to be seen whether he will take on the mantle of Ronaldo, who scored a world record 146 goals for Portugal. The longer-term favourite is Leao, an established star who has won Serie A with AC Milan. But Leao has hit a rough patch in the last couple of years and as his stock wanes, Forbs' star is only rising.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United hired Mauricio Pochettino as their next manager to replace Michael Carrick, who managed just one win in 10 games.

His appointment makes him Manchester United’s eighth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013.

Pochettino brings considerable Premier League experience after previous spells with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. He has also managed Paris Saint-Germain before the USA job.

As he faces Liverpool for his first game on Sunday, the question arises: is he facing the toughest job in the Premier League?

The question was posed on BBC Radio about who is going to have more pressure, Pochettino or Thomas Frank at Crystal Palace.

According to former Premier League defender Nedum Onuoha, the expectations surrounding Manchester United will make the Argentine’s job considerably harder.

Pochettino is preparing for his first game in charge of Manchester United, with Liverpool waiting at Anfield on November 22. However, the challenge facing the newly introduced manager goes beyond getting results on the pitch.

Onuoha believes Pochettino will have to deal with constant discussion and criticism about his work, much of it coming from former United players who are now in the media.

Choosing between Pochettino and Frank, Onuoha remarked, “Probably Pochettino, because every former Manchester United player works in the media, so there will always be discussion around what he is doing.

In a recent development, “Whereas Frank can just enjoy playing his football at Crystal Palace. If he does well then it is great, if he doesn’t do well then it is still OK.

“But from Pochettino’s perspective, if Manchester United finish the season 15th in the Premier League, whether we like it or not, there will be some criticism of him because he’s had 28 games to do something.”.

The comments just highlight the difference in expectations at the two clubs. Frank may have more freedom to work without the same level of attention, while Pochettino will be judged from day one against the standards historically associated with Manchester United. That is one substantial problem for Pochettino.

Recent findings suggest that rory Smith from The Observer highlighted another glaring problem at United. Highlighting a major problem, Smith remarked, “there is a cycle element to Manchester United whereby a manager comes in, makes things a bit better, and then within a year to 18 months they aren’t challenging for titles again because the Premier League has changed since they were a dominant force.”.

Pochettino’s first taste of action as a United manager will be against Liverpool at Anfield on November 22. That opening fixture will give him an immediate test, but the bigger task will be to get back United to winning ways, step by step.

It has been revealed that will the Manchester United job be without pressure for Mauricio Pochettino? Absolutely Not.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Championship has long been a breeding ground for exciting young talent, with the demands of the division providing an excellent test for some of English football's brightest prospects.

While experience, physicality, and consistency are often crucial ingredients for success at this level, there is certainly no shortage of youngsters making their mark during the 2026/27 Championship campaign.

Whether they are established starters already attracting attention from Premier League clubs, exciting loanees developing their reputations currently, or teenagers enjoying breakthrough seasons, the next generation is giving supporters plenty of reasons to be excited.

It has been revealed that some are already demonstrating the quality to become genuine difference-makers, while others are showing glimpses of the potential that could take them to the very top. There are plenty of candidates to consider, too.

The likes of Rabby Nzingoula, Adrian Segecic, Ryan Kavuma-McQueen, Jhon Solis, Sydie Peck, Ashley Phillips, Max Alleyne, Jimmy-Jay Morgan, Dastan Satpayev, and Rio Cardines are all deserving of honourable mentions.

Industry observers note that however, only 10 can make the final cut. We have already ranked the best players over 30 in the Championship, and these are the best Championship players aged 22 or below right now that Football League World have picked out.

Jovon Makama has continued to demonstrate why Norwich City were so keen to bring him to Carrow Road from Lincoln City in 2025.

Industry observers note that the 22-year-old enjoyed an encouraging first Championship campaign last season, scoring 10 league goals, and is showing that he can be a more than useful attacking option again when fit this term. His physical presence, willingness to run in behind, and powerful shot make him an interesting centre-forward, particularly given his potential to develop further.

He is not necessarily the finished article, but Norwich have a player who can cause problems for Championship defences and become an increasingly notable figure in their attack.

Despite their struggles, Bobby Clark is another exciting young player who has an opportunity to establish himself as a key figure at Championship level.

Having developed at Liverpool before joining Salzburg, he has already experienced different footballing environments despite his relatively young age. His technical ability, goal involvements, and capacity to operate in central midfield or further forward give Derby County some welcome versatility.

In a recent development, clark is comfortable receiving possession under pressure and looking to progress play, rather than simply keeping things ticking over. There is still plenty of development ahead of him, but his pedigree and technical qualities suggest Derby have secured a player with considerable scope to improve.

Mateus Mane is one of the most exciting teenage talents in English football and has already shown that he can compete against senior professionals at the highest level.

The 19-year-old possesses excellent dribbling ability, acceleration, and confidence when taking opponents on, making him a particularly dangerous option in wide areas.

Industry observers note that he is not afraid to attack defenders directly and has the technical quality to create opportunities for himself and his team-mates. Wolverhampton Wanderers have not seen the best of him yet this season, but he is a particularly exciting prospect on their hands, with Mane's potential so high. He can carry the ball and make things happen giving their attack a different dimension. His development will be worth monitoring closely, given his high ceiling.

Norwich have another exciting young forward in Mo Toure, whose goalscoring form has made him an increasingly vital part of their attacking options when fully fit.

The Australian arrived from Danish side Randers and has brought an impressive combination of pace, quality movement off the shoulder, and also electric finishing ability since his move to English football.

He has already demonstrated that he can be a real handful for Championship defenders, with five league goals in his first seven appearances this season. Toure is particularly dangerous when attacking space behind opposition defences, while his ability to finish chances with composure makes him an eye-catching prospect. Norwich could have a seriously valuable attacking asset on their hands.

Recent findings suggest that who is the most exciting young player in the Championship? Comment below!

Amario Cozier-Duberry has arguably been one of the most exciting attacking players in the Championship this season, with Middlesbrough benefiting enormously from his creativity and directness.

It has been revealed that having arrived from Brighton & Hove Albion on loan, the winger has promptly established himself as one of the division's major wide threats, combining excellent close control with the acceleration and confidence to beat defenders in one-on-one situations. His output has been particularly impressive, registering numerous goals and assists in his first league appearances.

At just 21, Cozier-Duberry looks capable of attracting serious Premier League interest or becoming a key player for Brighton.

Having excelled with Leicester City last season, Jordan James has already demonstrated that he possesses the qualities to become an excellent midfielder, having enjoyed an impressive campaign with a side relegated.

His 11 goals and four assists in 34 appearances highlighted his ability to contribute in the final third, but there is considerably more to his game than simply arriving in goalscoring positions.

The Welsh international combines physicality, energy, and the ability to crash the box, making him an effective presence in central midfield. Wolves have secured his services on a loan-to-buy deal from Rennes, giving him another opportunity to demonstrate his ability at this level before they trigger a clause to buy a player with plenty of room to develop.

Another loanee from the Premier League is Divine Mukasa, but the Man City loanee is a particularly exciting talent, with West Ham United giving the teenager an opportunity to develop his game in the Championship rather than simply remaining on the fringes of their senior squad.

Sources indicate that the 19-year-old is technically gifted, comfortable receiving possession in tight spaces, and possesses the vision to play progressive passes and break opposition lines. He has also demonstrated that he can contribute goals, scoring some stunning goals in the league this season.

Sources indicate that his ability to dictate possession and operate between the lines makes him an interesting creative option, while his maturity on the ball is impressive for someone so young. West Ham have a special prospect for this season at least.

Goalkeepers do not always receive the same recognition as exciting attacking youngsters, but Pierce Charles deserves his place in this selection.

Industry observers note that the Northern Ireland international has taken an crucial step in his development after joining QPR on loan from Man City, becoming their first-choice goalkeeper and starting all Championship matches so far. At just 21, that experience is particularly valuable, especially given the demands of playing regularly in such a competitive division.

He has already recorded clean sheets and made plenty of saves but it is his ability to contribute as an extra man in possession which is so impressive. Charles has plenty of development ahead of him, but QPR have an exciting young goalkeeper destined to be a Premier League regular one day.

Fer Lopez is another technically gifted young player who has brought plenty of creativity to Wolves' attacking options.

The Spaniard is particularly comfortable operating in the pockets of space between opposition midfield and defensive lines, where his close control, awareness, and ability to play incisive passes while also contributing to goals is already causing considerable problems to Championship opposition.

He also possesses the confidence to take defenders on and make things happen individually rather than relying entirely on team-mates. His return of goals and assists in his appearances so far underline his attacking contribution. At 22, Lopez has an extremely bright future.

Without a doubt, Will Lankshear has been the standout young goalscorer in the Championship this season, with Middlesbrough benefiting enormously from his arrival on loan from Tottenham Hotspur.

According to recent reports, the 21-year-old has been absolutely prolific, scoring at a rate of a almost a goal a game for Boro across all competitions. That has established himself as one of the division's most dangerous centre-forwards, let alone one of the best 22 and under.

It has been revealed that his movement inside the penalty area, willingness to attack crosses, and natural finishing ability off either foot has made him an outstanding acquisition for Kim Hellberg. He has also demonstrated that he can deliver consistently rather than simply enjoying an occasional purple patch. Boro have a serious talent on their hands for now.

A professional 1-0 victory at Lincoln City extended Wrexham’s unbeaten run to three games, having drawn with Wolves and secured a statement win over table-topping Middlesbrough.

According to recent reports, inconsistency has plagued the Red Dragons’ campaign so far though, struggling to rekindle the fine form which saw them go within touching distance of the Championship play-off places last season. But, Phil Parkinson’s side now appear to have found their feet.

After bringing an end to their five-game winless away run with a victory at Lincoln City, Wrexham are slowly but surely climbing the table and sit in 14th ahead of a trip to face a troubled Bristol City side.

The Robins have lost three on the bounce with pressure mounting on under-fire boss Michael Skubala after another underwhelming showing against Middlesbrough, although the Bristol City hierarchy have publicly backed him to turn them around.

Industry observers note that injuries have played a significant role in Wrexham’s slow start to the campaign, with influential forwards Josh Windass and Nathan Broadhead among those sidelined. Both are expected to return to action next month.

Question marks surround whether Oliver Rathbone will feature at Ashton Gate after being withdrawn on Saturday with a dead leg. Thankfully, Parkinson confirmed after the game that it isn’t a serious concern.

Callum O’Hare hasn’t featured since the defeat to Blackburn Rovers last month and remains a doubt with an ankle problem, while Sam Smith is a long-term absentee with an ACL injury.

In better news, New Zealand international Liberato Cacace, who is yet to make an appearance this term due to recurring calf injuries, is back in training.

Sebastian Revan is also nearing a return having been sidelined with a serious hamstring injury suffered on loan at Burton Albion in February. The 23-year-old is expected to be fit in the Newly introduced Year.

Patterson; Cleworth, Worrall, Doyle; Kabore, Whiteman, Dobson, Thomason; O’Brien, Rathbone; Moore.

The Wrexham side has remained largely unchanged since their much-needed victory over Middlesbrough, with Parkinson seemingly settled on his preferred starting team.

Anthony Patterson will be in goal after two clean sheets from his last three games. Max Cleworth has impressed recently with the experienced Joe Worrall alongside him and both will keep their places alongside standout performer Callum Doyle.

The Red Dragons’ positive form has coincided with Issa Kabore finding his stride in a right-wing back position, which saw him register an assist against Wolves. George Thomason has been equally key on the opposite flank and netted the winner at Lincoln, so both start again.

The midfield pivot of Ben Whiteman and George Dobson remains too, despite Ben Sheaf pushing for a place. Lewis O’Brien and Oliver Rathbone will be keen to impress once again in more advanced positions with Wrexham’s wealth of attacking talent waiting to return from injury.

They were sweating on the fitness of Kieffer Moore ahead of the trip to Sincil Bank, but he played the full 90 minutes at Sincil Bank and will likely lead the line.

Ex- Swindon Town, Burnley and QPR striker Charlie Austin has offered his services to the Robins after his former side dismissed Ian Holloway off the back of four straight defeats in all competitions.

Holloway has been under the magnifying glass ever since the start of the season, following a total collapse last year, which saw his side fall from second to completely missing the play-offs in the final 15 games.

Despite an okay start to the current League Two campaign, especially at home, just two wins in 15 in all competitions have put the self-proclaimed 'dead man walking' to rest, with a 2-0 away defeat at Newport County proving the fatal blow.

Now, Swindon are searching for a new boss, and a fan favourite on the pitch has stated that he is "free and available to help" turn things around in any sense.

Charlie Austin's affiliation with Swindon needs no introduction. The 37-year-old's EFL career began at the County Ground, with the Robins plucking him from non-league side Poole Town in 2009, aged 20.

From there, Austin spent 18 months before securing a move to Burnley, where he'd become an established Championship and Premier League frontman, before returning to Swindon midway through the 2022/23 campaign to end his professional career.

His final EFL season actually saw him play in every game for the Robins three years ago, and following the departure of Ian Holloway, the former striker took to X to offer his services to his former side.

"I am free and available to help," Austin tweeted, with the proximity to Holloway's dismissal implying that this is regarding the vacancy at the County Ground.

Austin hasn't shied away from his desire to get into coaching after his playing career came to an end. He publicly spoke about how he didn't get accepted into the QPR academy coaching team back in August.

This is a lot different from an academy role, but it reaffirms that aspiration to get into the dugout in some capacity in the near future.

The general vagueness of the tweet has sparked mixed reactions across X. However, when you sieve through fans questioning whether the 37-year-old can put his boots on and play for their team, or paint their living room, some Swindon supporters have reacted.

Most have taken the "free" part of Austin's tweet and used it to mock their current owner, Clem Morfuni, who they're at the moment not too happy with.

It has been revealed that "Being free is great because that fits morfuni's budget! Happy with Gav [Gunning] as your assistant?" one Swindon fan questioned. "Free !! That’s music to our owners ears," another remarked.

Others wondered what a Charlie Austin coaching staff would look like, and questioned if other players from their 2009/10 squad, which made the League One play-offs, could join him.

Industry observers note that "Get the band back together? Austin, [Billy] Paynter, [Simon] Ferry, [Jon-Paul] McGovern and [Phil] smithy as GK coach 🤣🤣," one fan tweeted.

Austin may not be the man to succeed Ian Holloway in the Swindon dugout. Every manager has to start somewhere, but hiring the former striker to his first role would be a massive risk.

But bringing him in as part of a fresh-look coaching staff may not be the craziest thing that the club has done. The 37-year-old is a popular figure among Swindon fans, and having him back at the club in a coaching capacity could help restore some good feelings at the County Ground.

Do you think Charlie Austin could return to Swindon Town in a coaching capacity? Let us know in the comments.

Swindon have had a miserable 11 months or so, and while they aren't looking over their shoulders at the bottom two, they need a pick-me-up, and they're still at a point in the season where the right hire can oversee a push towards promotion.

All eyes will be on whom the higher-ups at the County Ground turn to next, but perhaps they may take up Austin's offer in his tweet in doing so?

Pochettino’s first game comes against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday. His immediate priority will be to get some results for Manchester United but beyond the immediate games and results, Manchester United are expected to make multiple exits from the club as Pochettino settles into the job.

West Ham United will travel to Fratton Park for the first time in 14 years for Tuesday's Championship clash against Portsmouth.

The Hammers head into the midweek round of fixtures in 10th place, while the hosts are a point behind in 12th spot in the Championship table.

Portsmouth are sitting four points adrift of the top eight after winning six, drawing five and losing five of their 16 league games this term.

Pompey put together a six-game unbeaten run before they fell to a narrow 2-1 defeat in their most recent home outing before the international break.

John Mousinho's side then returned to action with an underwhelming display in Saturday's 1-1 away draw against Bolton Wanderers, which saw Josh Murphy score the opener with what proved to be Pompey's only shot on target.

Murphy's first goal since March 2025 was soon called out by Sam Dalby as Portsmouth played out a third consecutive away draw after previously taking a point from trips to Wolverhampton Wanderers and Burnley.

Portsmouth will now return to the familiar surroundings of Fratton Park, where they have won four of their last six outings since losing their opening two home games.

That mentioned, they will be looking to tighten up their backline if they are to take anything off the league's highest scorers, having recorded just one clean sheet in their eight outings at Fratton Park.

Meanwhile, West Ham have significant work to do if they are to secure an immediate return to the Premier League in their first Championship campaign since 2011-12.

The West Ham hierarchy took the decision to sack Nuno Espirito Santo after being underwhelmed by a return of six wins from the opening 13 league matches of the season.

Former Hammers midfielder Scott Parker has since taken over the reins, but he is still waiting to secure his first win after over two draws and one defeat in his first three matches.

After starting his reign with a comeback 3-3 draw against Cardiff City, Parker saw his side fall to a narrow 2-1 loss against Blackburn Rovers, before his charges returned from the international break with a frustrating 1-1 draw against Championship's basement side Preston North End.

As a result, West Ham have now gone five games without a win since recording back-to-back away victories over Lincoln City and Swansea City, leaving them three points adrift of the playoff spots and eight points away from the top two.

In search of inspiration, the Hammers can take confidence from the fact they have already beaten Portsmouth at home in the EFL Cup this season, and have won two of their previous three head-to-head away games - a 4-1 success in December 2008 (a game that Parker started) and a 1-0 victory in January 2012.

West Ham United Championship form:.

Portsmouth’s lengthy absentee list features Marko Milovanovic, Colby Bishop, Luke Brooke-Smith, Keshi Anderson, John Swift, Mark Kosznovszky, Benjamin Arthur and Connor Ogilvie.

Jayden Meghoma is a doubt after being forced off in the closing stages against Bolton with an ankle problem, while a calf concern prevented Marlon Pack from starting Saturday’s draw.

Mousinho will welcome back midfielder Ebou Adams, who has served his one-match ban for an accumulation of yellow cards.

As for the visitors, they are unable to call upon Kyle Walker-Peters and Keiber LaMadrid due to muscle and knee problems respectively.

Goalkeeper Alphonse Areola remains a doubt after sitting out Saturday’s draw with an injury he sustained in the pre-match warm-up against Blackburn earlier this month.

Defender Max Kilman is expected to come into the back four after completing his one-match suspension for accumulating five yellow cards in the Championship.

Portsmouth possible starting lineup:.

Schmid; Devlin, Poole, Dia, Swanson; Adams, Mohamed; Segecic, Bailey, Kamara; Shade.

West Ham United possible starting lineup:.

Herrick; Veltman, Mavropanos, Kilman, Mayers; Alvarez; Bowen, Engels, Mukasa, Solomon; Taty.

While West Ham lost their last away game against Blackburn, that result represents their only defeat in their eight Championship road trips this season, so we expect them to take something from this midweek encounter.

However, we think they will be forced to settle for a point against a Portsmouth side that has lost just one of their previous eight matches.

Blackburn Rovers travelled to bitter rivals Burnley on Sunday afternoon aiming to claim all three points despite Tony Mowbray's absence, and though they didn't achieve their goal, they undoubtedly made their manager proud.

Blackburn were rocked by the news last week of Mowbray's sudden decision to step back from his role at the helm at Ewood Park, citing health problems as his reasoning.

Damien Johnson and Mike Dodds have since assumed control of the Rovers squad, and heading into Sunday's crucial clash with Burnley in the Championship, the Blackburn squad looked to make their manager proud, and they did.

Industry observers note that burnley took the lead just before the half-hour mark courtesy of a strike from Belgian winger Largie Ramazani. However, the Clarets lead didn't last long, as Andri Gudjohnsen did what he does best and fired home an equaliser just four minutes later.

In his celebration, Gudjohnsen held a shirt showing support for Mowbray, along with his Blackburn teammates, to the camera, in a touching tribute to the 62-year-old who previously beat bowel cancer.

Burnley would again take the lead in the 51st minute thanks to Dutch winger Jayden Banel, but Blackburn were insistent on not leaving empty-handed, as Gudjohnsen won a penalty which Todd Cantwell converted with 15 minutes to go.

The game would ultimately end 2-2, as Blackburn have made Burnley wait even longer for a first home win in over 400 days, as the players' support and admiration for Mowbray has grown increasingly evident after full-time.

Blackburn captain Cantwell, who netted the equaliser, joined in his side's celebrations for the first goal and subsequent support of Mowbray, and following the game, the former Norwich City forward has released a message to his gaffer via Instagram.

In a heartfelt message directed towards Mowbray, Cantwell claims that the squad admire and respects the 62-year-old greatly, before going on to acknowledge his impact on the team and everyone at the club.

Blackburn sit 13th in the Championship table after this fixture, and being five points off the play-offs and 11 clear of the relegation zone, have silenced some critics.

As for now, Johnson and Dodds will lead the club forward while Mowbray recovers; as Blackburn are not looking for a permanent successor right now, Mowbray's philosophy and leadership will continue to reign over Ewood Park.

Industry observers note that what do you make of Todd Cantwell's message for Tony Mowbray? Does Blackburn have what it takes to find success without him right now at the helm? Share your thoughts below!

Looking ahead to the summer, Blackburn have numerous contract issues to address sooner rather than later, with 13 players set to leave the club on a free transfer in 2027, including Cantwell.

Along with the Englishman, Balazs Toth, Oladapo Afolayan, Yuki Ohashi, and Harry Pickering also see their current deals expire, though the latter two reportedly have one-year extension clauses in their contracts.

Regardless, attention must turn to these contract situations sooner rather than later at Ewood Park, especially in the case of Cantwell, who has been consistently one of Blackburn's best players over the past few years.

His importance to the club cannot be measured, and it would be a disaster to allow him to leave for nothing, as this is an glitch that must be addressed ASAP.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There were a few modern-day Blackburn Rovers legends in attendance at Turf Moor on Sunday, as the spoils were shared in the Cotton Mills derby.

Burnley led twice in the game through goals from Largie Ramazani and Jaydon Banel, but were pegged back both times by Andri Gudjohnsen and Todd Cantwell from the penalty spot.

Neither side were able to find a winner, though, meaning that the Clarets' winless league run at home surpasses 400 days and 23 games, equaling the English record set by Sheffield Wednesday last season.

It also means that Blackburn are still without a win over their East Lancashire rivals since March 2010, and despite how disjointed this past week must have been, given the news that Tony Mowbray had to step back from his role as head coach for health reasons, some critics, and Burnley fans especially, felt this to be a missed opportunity for the away side.

That didn't stop Blackburn fans from having fun at a ground they rarely pick up points at, and former players were in attendance to enjoy the occasion with them.

David Bentley, who spent three seasons at Ewood Park between 2005 and 2008, during which he made the majority of his seven England caps, was in the away end and led chants in the concourse, and after the game, he linked up with former Premier League winner Collin Hendry and his ex-Blackburn teammate Brad Friedel.

Sources indicate that friedel, who is the upcoming sporting director at League Two side Shrewsbury Town, was also part of those squads under Mark Hughes alongside Bentley. Blackburn finished sixth, tenth and seventh in those three seasons, making the semi-finals of the EFL Cup in 2006 and the FA Cup in 2007.

The American goalkeeper's time at Blackburn extended before Bentley's, too, and at Ewood Park, he helped get the side back into the Premier League in 2001 and won the EFL Cup in 2002.

It may have been close to 20 years since they both last played for Blackburn, but they're still iconic amongst the fanbase, and they had some fun with the Rovers fans as they were made to stay back after full-time.

Blackburn fans were joyous in that away end at Turf Moor on Sunday, even despite not picking up all three points, and were happy to see their former players in attendance, too.

Bentley, especially, was living the fans' dream in the Cotton Mills derby, both in the stands and on the pitch after the game, and Blackburn supporters enjoyed being with him during the game.

"Gotta love Bentley," one fan commented. "I want some of what he drinks every day! What a geezer 🤩," another remarked.

Sources indicate that A third commented on the link-up with Friedel, reminding them of their last truly glorious era at Ewood Park, before this current spell in the EFL, saying, "This is the Blackburn of Mark Hughes. Missing them old days.".

Recent findings suggest that what do you think about David Bentley's actions after the game? Let us know in the comments.

However, there were plenty of Burnley fans in the replies to the Blackburn tweet, too, reminding them that they hadn't won in the derby, and likely shouldn't be celebrating the point so hard, given how dire the Clarets have been so far this season.

"Congratulations on the draw lads 👏 👏," one Burnley fan replied. "Celebrating like they’ve won the league not just drawn with possibly the worst Burnley teams in 30 years," another mentioned.

"Can’t wait to tell the grandkids about that famous 2-2 win at Burnley, even better than the 1-1 win last time," was also among the reactions from Clarets fans. Evidently, with just one league win all season, they don't think Blackburn should be getting too giddy about leaving Turf Moor with just a point.

Ultimately, Blackburn don't beat Burnley often, so when a decent result away from home can come about, they'll more than enjoy themselves, especially if some former players from a better period in the club's history are in attendance.

Also, Rovers avoided what could have been one of their most embarrassing defeats in the derby, handing their rivals only their second win of the season and their first win at home in 400 days.

Given the expectation for them to win, plus the clearly hectic week they've had since Mowbray had to step down and the fact they had to come from behind twice in the game, a point isn't the end of the world, and it helps them maintain their 11-point gap on Burnley in 22nd.

Perhaps they'll look back on the game now and feel it's an opportunity missed to end a 16-year derby hoodoo, but at the time, it was a fine point, and those in the away end evidently enjoyed their day out; David Bentley, especially.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Towards the end of the Australian summer of 2014-15, as the country prepared to host the Cricket World Cup, I took a flight from Sydney to Hobart, Tasmania, to watch a Sheffield Shield game between Tasmania and Fresh South Wales at the Bellerive Oval, a beautiful ground perched on the banks of the Derwent River.
  • Recent findings suggest that australian sport was still in shock.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 22:15 EST, 19 November 2026.

Towards the end of the Australian summer of 2014-15, as the country prepared to host the Cricket World Cup, I took a flight from Sydney to Hobart, Tasmania, to watch a Sheffield Shield game between Tasmania and Fresh South Wales at the Bellerive Oval, a beautiful ground perched on the banks of the Derwent River.

Recent findings suggest that australian sport was still in shock. A few months earlier, Australia's Test opener, Phillip Hughes, had died after he was struck on the side of his neck by a short ball from a young bowler called Sean Abbott in a game between Fresh South Wales and South Australia at the Sydney Cricket Ground.

Hughes was treated at the ground for 40 minutes and then taken by ambulance to St Vincent's Hospital in nearby Darlinghurst in a critical condition. 'Feeling for Phil Hughes after being hit,' former Australia Test cricketer Dean Jones wrote on Twitter. 'He is not in a good way! Stay strong Sean Abbott. Not your fault, young man.'.

The impact of the ball had compressed a vein in Hughes' neck and when it split, it caused a catastrophic bleed on the brain. Hughes had emergency surgery and was placed in an induced coma. He never regained consciousness and passed away two days later.

Hughes was a popular, talented, gutsy cricketer with three Test centuries already under his belt. A small guy with the heart of a lion. He was 25 years old. Cricket mourned a terrible tragedy – some called it the sport's saddest day and the agony of Hughes' family was hard to bear. But there was something else. There was an awareness that two tragedies were playing out in front of us.

Recent findings suggest that hughes was lost but the man who had bowled the delivery that felled him had been left behind, desolate and distraught. Many thought Sean Abbott, who was 22, would never play cricket again. That he would not be able to find the strength. But that was why I had flown to Tasmania. Because Abbott had found the strength.

Phil Hughes was the golden boy of Australian cricket in 2014, with three Test centuries already to his name, when he was hit by a ball bowled by Sean Abbott and died.

Abbott visiting the Sydney hospital where Hughes was in a coma that he would never wake from, having suffered a catastrophic bleed on the brain.

That February afternoon at the Bellerive Oval, I sat among a smattering of spectators who watched Abbott walk to the top of his mark. His team-mates shouted encouragement to him. They were willing him on with everything they had and Abbott bowled his heart out.

It has been revealed that 'Beautifully bowled, Abbo,' one of the NSW fielders shouted after one ball to former Test opener Ed Cowan. 'That's a beauty, Seanie,' another yelled after the fifth ball of his first over, when Cowan jerked his head out of the way of a short delivery so fast he fell over. Only one wicket fell that afternoon. Abbott took it.

It was one of the bravest sporting performances I have ever witnessed. Because even though cricket had voiced its support for Abbott, the sport could not protect him from his thoughts and from the knowledge he had become one of a cursed band of sportsmen who have unwittingly caused the death of an opponent during a contest.

Industry observers note that sometimes, tragedy in sport is not just the tragedy of the player who dies; it is the tragedy of the opponent who must live the nightmare of what he has done over and over again in his mind. To those that it has befallen, they say it is a grief that never leaves them.

That grief, that sense of a double tragedy, was brought sharply back into focus earlier this month when Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died in hospital the day after a sickening collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono. The accident happened in the final minutes of a game in Spain's Segunda Division, when Owono hurtled out of his goal and collided with De Miguel in the centre circle. He was shown a red card for the foul.

Recent findings suggest that there was an outpouring of grief for De Miguel. I was among those who observed a minute's silence for him before the Barcelona-Aston Villa Champions League tie at the Nou Camp the next evening. Tributes continue to be paid to him. Owono, meanwhile, has become a pariah. It is remarked that the 25-year-old rarely leaves his house.

Recent findings suggest that owono does not appear to have had the same sympathy extended to him that Abbott benefited from. His challenge on De Miguel, a striker who had had a peripatetic career in Spain's lower leagues, was reckless and cavalier. For him, the struggle with guilt and responsibility and public judgment is only just beginning.

FC Andorra will play their first home game since the tragedy against Leganes on Friday night but when they run out at the Encamp Stadium, a neat little ground beside a babbling river, the Valira d'Orient, and in the shadow of the mountains that make Andorra such a popular ski resort, Owono will not be there.

Earlier this month Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died in hospital the day after a sickening collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono.

Industry observers note that owono has become a pariah. It is said that the 25-year-old rarely leaves his house.

The goalkeeper, who has 47 caps for Equatorial Guinea, was given the maximum sentence of a 12-match ban by the Spanish Football Federation.

Tenerife manager Alvaro Cervera suggested Owono's ban 'might feel light' to all those mourning the striker, who was 30 years old, while FC Andorra owner Gerard Pique, the former Barcelona and Spain centre back, said the maximum sanction 'puts him (Owono) in a situation he does not deserve, because he is not to blame for all of this having happened'.

According to recent reports, no one knows whether Owono will feel able to return to football when his ban ends. Footage circulated of him in an on-field argument moments before the clash with De Miguel, and it was used to suggest that he was in an unstable state of mind.

Some have pressed for him to be charged with manslaughter. His Instagram account was deactivated after it was deluged with abuse, including messages which branded him 'a murderer'. It has been reported that his brother, who is also a footballer, has been the victim of abuse because of his association with Owono.

It has been revealed that owono has only communicated through a statement released by his club. 'These are the most difficult days of my life,' he wrote. 'I struggle to find the words, and I find it very hard to ​process what has happened. I feel enormous pain at the loss of Jesus. I think of him, his family, and all the people who loved him. I know there will be many questions to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect.'.

I spoke to the great British fighter Barry McGuigan about Owono this week. McGuigan has suffered his share of tragedies. His brother, Dermot, took his own life. He lost his daughter, Danika, to cancer when she was just 33, in 2019. And in 1982, three years before he won the world featherweight title at Loftus Road, he nearly quit boxing altogether.
