📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mauricio Pochettino is fighting a losing battle after stating that Manchester United deserved a penalty in their 4-0 defeat to Liverpool.
  • That is according to former PGMOL chief and ex-FIFA referee, Keith Hackett, who exclusively told Football Insider that Bryan Mbeumo attempted to con the referee into awarding a spot-kick.
  • Two minutes before Leny Yoro was sent off at Anfield on Sunday, 22 November, the Red Devils had a penalty shout of their own at the other end.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino is fighting a losing battle after stating that Manchester United deserved a penalty in their 4-0 defeat to Liverpool.

That is according to former PGMOL chief and ex-FIFA referee, Keith Hackett, who exclusively told Football Insider that Bryan Mbeumo attempted to con the referee into awarding a spot-kick.

Two minutes before Leny Yoro was sent off at Anfield on Sunday, 22 November, the Red Devils had a penalty shout of their own at the other end.

Mbeumo, who had burst into the Liverpool box, threw himself to the floor under pressure from Jeremy Jacquet, who went shoulder-to-shoulder with the attacker.

Sam Barrott waved away the shouts, with VAR refusing to get involved either, and then Man United self-imploded near their own penalty box.

After the game, Pochettino was absolutely adamant that Mbeumo should have been awarded a spot-kick, but very few appear to agree with him.

Speaking exclusively to Football Insider, Hackett, instead of taking Pochettino's side, has accused Mbeumo of an "exaggerated fall".

"I don't think that's enough for a penalty for me. I think the referee got it right. What creates the debate, if you like, is Mbeumo's exaggerated fall," he stated.

"Players have just got to go down naturally and not exaggerate. So for me, I I didn't see that as a penalty kick decision.".

When asked if Pochettino was "clutching at straws," he added: "He'll probably receive, at some stage in the coming weeks, operational advice on what he can and cannot say.".

Such split-second decisions can have major impacts on a game at this level. Luckily for Barrott, it seems he made the right one on this occasion.

Yoro's red card, undoubtedly, changed the game completely, with Liverpool able to stroll comfortably to a 4-0 win at home.

There has been a huge debate over the decision, and Hackett is not entirely sure that sending the defender off was the right call.

It was a subjective one, and that's exactly why the former boss of the PGMOL believes that Man United have a case to appeal the red card.

It remains to be seen if the Red Devils are going to bother, but the news would certainly be a significant boost, with the team presently in the relegation zone.

Breaking: An inspiral of a star inside a common envelope with its giant companion

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 41 min read (8138 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~41 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the formation of compact stellar binaries requires rapid orbital tightening of their progenitor binary stars1,2.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the formation of compact stellar binaries requires rapid orbital tightening of their progenitor binary stars1,2. This is theorized to happen through common envelope evolution (CEE)3, when the stars orbit in a loosely bound, shared convective envelope, triggering an inspiral due to frictional drag4,5. However, this inspiral in such a system has never been observed directly. Here we present observations of AT 2025abao, a transient eruption in the Andromeda Galaxy, which originates from the CEE of an approximately 7M⊙ asymptotic giant branch (AGB) star with its companion. Extensive pre- and post-eruption spectroscopy is best explained as an approximately 0.7M⊙ companion inspiralling within the convective AGB envelope that powers a seven-year period of gradual brighteningone of the first direct observations of frictional drag energy dissipation induced by CEE. This phase is radiatively efficient, consistent with predictions for convective transport in CEE5,6,7,8. The subsequent merger of the companion with the primary core powers the ejection of the outermost 10% of the stellar envelope at speeds about 10× the primary escape speed, and empirically constrains the fraction of dissipated orbital energy available to unbind the convective common envelope4,9,10,11, 0.01 ≲ α ≲ 0.4. This end-to-end characterization using multi-survey observations demonstrates a path towards mapping the landscape of CEE outcomes with upcoming surveys.

It has been revealed that optical spectra of the AT 2025abao eruption. Its spectral evolution matches the characteristic evolution seen in LRNe — blue continuum with emission lines at early times that transitions to a red continuum with molecular absorption features at late times.

Near-infrared spectra of AT 2025abao, from its precursor phase (red) and the eruption (blue). The spectra during the precursor phase resemble late M-type stars, while those during the eruption shows a transition to hotter temperatures. Notably, the CO absorption bands are seen in all spectra, indicating that some molecular gas remains intact even after the eruption.

The black shaded region marks the range expected by varying stellar parameters in the analytical model (section ‘Comparisons to theoretical predictions of enhanced mass loss’). The observed dust mass from the archival progenitor SED and the JWST observation is shown in purple, which constrains the system mass ratio to \(q=0.1{0}_{-0.08}^{+0.10}\).

Previously identified sources such as V1309Sco, M31-LRN-2015, AT 2019zhd (circles) exhibit a gradual brightening by several magnitudes prior to its eruption. AT 2025abao (stars) differs from these sources, as it only shows a bumpy  ≈ 1 magnitude brightening before transitioning to its eruption.

Evolution of FWHM velocities inferred from our spectra (red), compared to theoretical expectations for momentum-conserving collisions with CBM following a ρ(r) ∝ r−2 density profile (blue solid line). The broken lines indicate the expectation by including an additional mechanical power source, such as a surviving binary, injecting momentum into the ejecta. Our observations constrain the magnitude of this power source \(\mathop{E}\limits^{.}\lesssim 1{0}^{40}\) erg s−1.

LRNe for which progenitor primary stars have been identified are plotted as coloured points, colour-coded by the binding energy of the star. LRNe with no progenitor identifications are plotted as grey points. The eruption of AT 2025abao (star) is remarkably similar to other LRNe, despite having a progenitor with the lowest binding energy ever measured.

a, The quiescent binary system comprising a  ≈ 7 M⊙ AGB and a  ≈ 0.7 M⊙ star, surrounded by an extended dust shell from mass loss from the binary following Roche Lobe overflow of the primary. b, The precursor brightening phase that began in 2018, marking the onset of CEE, powered by frictional drag on the inspiraling companion lasting for  ≈ 7 years. The mass outflow rate during this phase is  ~10−2 M⊙ yr−1, producing  ~0.1 M⊙ of CBM in an equatorial disk around the binary (dark brown). c, The ballistic eruption in late 2025 from the merger of the inspiraling companion with the primary core, resulting in the ejection of  ≈ 0.1 − 0.2 M⊙ of the primary envelope, and sublimation of a large fraction of dust around the binary. d, The eventual lightcurve powered by shock-interactions between freely expanding merger ejecta (indicated by yellow arrows) and equatorially focused CBM. The surviving pre-existing dust is traced by our JWST observations. The black arrows between the panels indicate the progression of time.

AC Milan consider Virgil van Dijk to be their number one defensive target ahead of next summer, and believe a deal is possible.

It has been revealed that according to a report from La Gazzetta dello Sport, Milan decided to explore the possibility of signing Van Dijk ahead of the current season as they looked at various options to bolster the centre-back department. However, the conditions were not present to go beyond simply being interested.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It has been revealed that the Dutchman turned 35 in July but remains one of the most highly-regarded defenders of his generation. The difference ahead of summer 2027 is that things might finally line up with Milan’s desire to allow him to experience a spell in Italy.

Virgil’s contract expires in June and he’s always been fascinated by the idea of a move to Milan and playing in Serie A. It’s still a complex negotiation to carry out, but at the moment Gerry Cardinale seems determined to try.

In addition to La Gazzetta’s report, The Touchline are reporting the following: “Virgil van Dijk is AC Milan’s dream signing! Milan want to make him their highest-paid player, give him the captain’s armband and build their defence around him.

“They see Van Dijk as the leader of a newly introduced era at San Siro. The idea is for him to set the standard in the dressing room, guide their younger defenders and lead a team built to challenge for the Serie A title and compete with Europe’s best.”.

Given the outlay planned to get Sporting CP captain Goncalo Inacio in January, it seems as though the Rossoneri are keen to build towards having the best defence in the country, which they are presently some way off.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea are starting to have serious doubts about Xabi Alonso's position as a result of a miserable recent run of form.

Despite a strong start to life under the Spaniard, Chelsea have now won just three of their last nine games across all competitions, sparking a growing list of concerns.

A 4-1 defeat against bitter rivals Leeds United at Stamford Bridge last time out has done little to calm the situation, and any Blues manager would face pressure after that result.

Former Man United chief scout Mick Brown told Football Insider that Alonso must turn around Chelsea's form rapidly or risk coming under fire from all angles.

Sections of the fanbase at Stamford Bridge have already begun to turn on the manager, and while the board are keen to support him long-term, they could soon follow suit.

Alonso has proven his managerial credentials in the past, but further defeats like the one against Leeds will only ramp up the pressure on his position at Chelsea.

Brown told Football Insider on 9 November that Chelsea do not have any significant concerns about Alonso's future in the position, and are backing him to turn things around.

The manager recently explained that the side we see now will not be the same one we see come the end of the season, but should these results continue, he may not oversee that change.

The heavy defeat against Leeds, coming just weeks after they lost against another major rival in Tottenham, has raised upcoming questions about Alonso's role in the dugout.

"Chelsea have been pretty keen to stick by Alonso, but that can only last for so long," Brown told Football Insider.

"Ultimately, the biggest influence on his position will be whether he's winning games or not, so when they're in this kind of form there will always be pressure on him.

"But a 4-1 defeat at home against Leeds would be a disaster for any Chelsea manager, and I expect they now have some serious doubts about his role in that.

"It was a shocking result and won't have gone down well with anybody at Chelsea.

"Chelsea fans have high expectations, so it's no surprise that they've started to turn on him, but I can see the board going that way too if things don't change rapidly.".

Doubts about Alonso's position have already grown amongst the Chelsea fans and hierarchy, and there are now concerns that the players are also facing concerns.

Football Insider revealed on 22 November that Alonso is facing a potential mutiny in his squad, with players questioning his decisions and methods on the training ground.

In the wake of a heavy defeat aganist Leeds, influential players are believed to have raised concerns, with discontent growing from within the Chelsea dressing room.

Alonso has only been in the job for a matter of months, but is already understood to be facing significant pressure on his position, and things must change quickly.

Liverpool 4-0 Man United: How "electric" Rio Ngumoha gave Andoni Iraola the big Anfield win he needed

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (303 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Lewis Nolan | 22 Nov 2026 18:40.
  • If Andoni Iraola had been allowed to write the script for this game, it would probably have played out in broadly similar fashion.
  • Liverpool came into their latest clash with bitter rivals Manchester United having enjoyed a healthy start under the Basque, yet with a few question marks still over them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Nolan | 22 Nov 2026 18:40.

Written by David Lynch, Liverpool expert:.

If Andoni Iraola had been allowed to write the script for this game, it would probably have played out in broadly similar fashion.

Liverpool came into their latest clash with bitter rivals Manchester United having enjoyed a healthy start under the Basque, yet with a few question marks still over them.

That is exactly why this victory was extra sweet for Iraola, because his team answered each of them across the course of an enjoyable afternoon at Anfield.

The first concerned a poor home record that had seen the Reds take just five points from a possible 15, and which was clearly enhanced here.

The second related to their record in massive games thanks to recent defeats to Manchester City and Arsenal.

Yes, United are in a tricky spot at the moment, but it can never be remarked that a meeting between England's two biggest clubs is not 'major'.

The third, meanwhile, was about whether Liverpool had shown enough in terms of free-flowing football, and they surely answered that in tearing the Red Devils apart here, largely through the electric Rio Ngumoha.

Clearly, it would be remiss not to mention Leny Yoro's early sending off as a decisive moment in the contest and the hosts' bid to tick certain boxes.

But judgement of Liverpool's issues this term has hardly been dripping in nuance, with key refereeing decisions against both City and Arsenal ignored, for example.

As such, it is surely only fair to take this result and performance at face value, as Iraola and his players likely will.

That means they will come away from this afternoon feeling like they are a team building momentum under a latest manager, which is exactly what they are.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot currently “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

“We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

“We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”.

Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz.

Alisson, Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo all made their first appearances and contributed to a lively first-half in which Iraola’s commitment to man-to-man marking and an intensive pressing structure were evident out of possession. With the ball in the first half they demonstrated the kind of slick passing that Bournemouth employed to carve opponents open on the counter-attack.

A nimble one-two between Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai allowed the Dutch midfielder to set up Alexander Isak to score with a shot from 16 yards and the most expensive player in English football history laid claim to the second, too, when he seemed to hook in a rebound from Lukas Hradecky’s save while lying in the six-yard box.

Later he would graciously acknowledge that he and Florian Wirtz had connected with the ball simultaneously and he was happy to yield the credit to his team-mate.

Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw.

Recent findings suggest that at that point it seemed that victory would be a cakewalk but just before half-time Aleksandr Golovin caught Van Dijk out with a feint and late swerve to the right, tripping over the Liverpool captain’s clumsy hack. Despite a heavy limp, Golovin hammered the penalty past Alisson’s dive to make it 2-1 at the break.

Iraola rationed his early changes at the start of the second half to two but Liverpool could not regain their rhythm and Mika Biereth capitalised on a Gravenberch error to score the equaliser after battling to be first to the rebound when Giorgi Mamardashvili saved his first effort, stroking his effort through Wataru Endo’s legs.

Industry observers note that cue five substitutions as soon as that goal had gone in and a raft more followed, killing the remaining half-hour of all momentum and cohesion. By the time Brunner exploited a dozy mix-up between Milos Kerkez and Federico Chiesa about whose responsibility he was at a corner to flash his header past Mamardashvili, only two of the 22 starters were still on the pitch.

Recent findings suggest that liverpool: Alisson (Mamardashvili 46), Tsimikas (Kerkez 59), Van Dijk (c) (Chambers 59), Ndukwe (Endo 46), Frimpong (Ramsay 75), Gravenberch (Nyoni 59), Gakpo (Ngumoha 59), Wirtz (McConnell 59), Koumas (Chiesa 75), Isak (Muñoz 59)Substitutes: Morrison, Davies.Goals: Isak (16), Wirtz (29)Monaco: Hradecky, Nazinho (Mawissa 75), Dier (c) (Kehrer 75), S Sané, Vanderson (Teze 46), Golovin (Idumbo 75), Cabral (Soubeir 75), Camara (Benzahra 64), Detourbet (Coulibaly 64), Biereth (Brunner 80), Abline (Konaté 64).Substitutes: Assab, Kohn, Lienard, Nibombe, Touré. Goals: Golovin (44 pen), Biereth (56), Brunner (88).

They played well in the first half, as they did against Leeds, but lost all shape and structure in the second half to lose 3-2.

According to recent reports, yellow card for Konate for clattering into Endo late. That’s the last of the action.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 3 (Brunner)  Brilliant near-post glancing header from a devilishly whippy, dipping corner. Kerkez doing his best Rip van Winkle impression.

Diligent defensive work by Ngumoha stops Konate’s run down the outside left.

As usual, the substitutions have killed the game. Watched Leeds vs RB Leipzig yesterday. They played two 60 minute matches which kept it more competitive for longer but still descended into a kickabout late on.

Mawissa, Kehrer, Idumbo and Soubeir have replaced Nazinho, Dier, Golovin and Cabral.

According to recent reports, monaco also made changes, four I think. Will catch up with then once they’re confirmed. Ramsey is into the game straight away tp stop Coulibaly’s shot.

That would have stung. Good save. A flag would have meant it wouldn’t have counted but even so Frimpong’s defensive work wasn’t good enough.

Three changes for Monaco with Detoubet, Abline and Camara departing for Benzhara, Coulibaly and Konaté.

Monaco overplay at the edge of the box, Detourbet, Biereth and Abline playing ‘after you. Claud’, instead of shooting.

It has been revealed that A slick, short passing move between Gravenberch, Wirtz and Isak ends with Isak on the deck in the box after Gravenberch’s step-over allowed the ball to run to him. Isak took a touch to move the ball on to his left but gave the defender a glimmer of it and he hacked it away before felling Isak as well as collateral damage.

Liverpool try to play out from the back with Mamardashvili spearing a straight pass to Gravenberch who tried to knock it round the corner for Endo but the ball skidded under his studs and out for a throw-in.

Much to admire in that first-half performance from Liverpool’s front six and centre-backs, the latter two particularly out of possession and winning it back. The man-to-man system is working well for them. But they should be out of sight by now instead of leading by only a goal.

Liverpool free-kick on the right after a foul on Koumas. Szoboszlai whips in the cross and Van Dijk gets up first to the left of the penalty spot but bludgeons his header about a foot wide of the right post.

Charlie Adam claims the penalty was ‘a soft one’ but Van Dijk did not adjust when Golovin shifted it to his right, stuck out a leg and Golovim understandably decided to topple over the hurdle.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 1 (Golovin, pen) Speared it into the top right. Alisson went the right way but was beaten for pace and power.

Industry observers note that the referee, Jarred Gillett, gives Monaco a penalty. It was deserved, too. Golovin went on a driving run down the middle, shifted it to his right and was tripped by Van Dijk.

In a recent development, liverpool are well worth their lead. They are streets ahead of Monaco.

A microcosm of the game so far: Liverpool pass goes astray, a player wins it back – this time Gakpo – by snapping into a tackle before laying it off to his left for the unmarked Tsimikas to skim a low shot about a foot wide of the left post from 25 yards.

Monaco have done very little since that wee salvo in the opening minute but just now Abline was given too much space from distance but whacked his shot into the Kop.

Significant cheer from the crowd for Hugo Ekitike.

Gakpo meets it with a header back across goal to Isak whose first effort from a couple of yards is blocked but the ball gets stuck under Isak’s falling body and Wirtz is Johnny on the Spot to stab it in from a 18 inches as Dier tried to scramble it away.

Industry observers note that liverpool have been impressive so far but if there has been a weakness it’s still the balance in central midfield defensively. Liverpool 1 Monaco 0 (Isak) Chip to Gakpo down the left of the box, he clips it first time back to Gravenberch in the D who lays it off to Szoboszlai. Ping-ping-ping. Charlie Adam on co-comms points out that Liverpool are going man-to-man now in classic Iraola/Bielsa style and when the camera goes high you can see it, especially with the full-backs.

Liverpool defend the corner solidly and Frimpong races away on the counter, bombing on to the ball and sprinting into the Monaco half. But his touch is not as sound as his pace and Monaco deal with him when he fluffs his control.

A period of applause in memory of Kevin Keegan ❤️ pic.twitter.com/AkPZG7babe.

They roll the ball back to Frimpong who chips a long pass up the right to Koumas who hares on to the pass down the right and crosses, just beyond Isak. Hradecky gathers and bowls the ball out. A mistake by Tisimikas lets Biereth barrel through the inside-right to hammer a shot that Alisson turns behind for a corner.

Recent findings suggest that the crowd applauds in the modern way. My goodness he was a terrific player. Saw him play for Liverpool, Southampton and Newcastle. Absolutely relentless.

For me it’s a special game, most of the players and people will be ‘it’s [just] a pre-season friendly’, but for me it’s a lot more than this. It will be the first time I have the chance to go out, to feel this stadium and I hope we can also perform well.

It’s a good game for us, because it’s going to be demanding, it’s a team that wants to dominate and they also want to press high so we will see how we are.

According to recent reports, I think the cases of Ali[sson], Cody, and Virgil I think it’s their first game. It shouldn’t go longer than 45 minutes, maybe a little bit more if they feel comfortable.

Also for some of the others Ryan, Flo, and Alex, it’s the second game so we have to be aware of those things.

But the league starts in two weeks, so we cannot wait also too much; we have to give them quality minutes.

Sources indicate that I think today is going to be a good reference, two games – Monaco and Como – teams that try dominate the game, they are very good in possession, so they will demand us the best without the ball. If we want to control the game and also physical teams, they are probably a very good test.

I hope we are at the level and we can do very good games.

The Reds to take on AS Monaco at Anfield!Watch the match LIVE on All Red Video 📺.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the first of two Liverpool home friendlies after their preseason tour of the United States. Andoni Iraola’s side saw off Wrexham and Sunderland in their first two matches but gave away a two-goal lead at half-time in the final fixture and ended up being beaten 4-2 by Leeds United in Chicago in the last game after multiple changes. What did we learn? Not a huge amount in the absence of Virgil van Dijk, Alisson, Víctor Muñoz, Cody Gakpo and Alexis Mac Allister, the first four of whom are available today other than an ongoing vulnerability from set-pieces and Curtis Jones looking like he is in desperate need of a fresh start.

This afternoon at Anfield they take on AS Monaco who finished seventh in Ligue 1 this season but are under fresh management with the recruitment of the former Chelsea and Atlético left-back Filipe Luís as head coach. It’s quite the coup for Le Rocher given he led Flamengo to their first Brazilian title in five years, the Copa Libertadores and the Copa do Brasil in his 18 months in charge.

In pre-season so far he has overseen a 5-2 win over fourth-tier AS Saint-Priest, a 2-0 defeat by Sporting Clube, a 2-2 draw with Cercle Bruges and a 1-0 victory over Getafe. They have sold their best player, Maghnes Akliouche, to PSG for £43m and Aladji Bamba to Newcastle for £34m but have so far retained Mamadou Coulibaly and Folarin Balogun, signed and made Ansu Fati’s loan move into a long-term deal.

Iraola may well persevere with Trey Nyoni in midfield who, after his performances on tour, ought to be on the threshold of a breakthrough season and it would be interesting to see him paired with Ryan Gravenberch just behind Dominik Szoboszlai.

Ifeanyi Ndukwe, who played well in America after coming on for the injured Joe Gomez, does not have a UK work permit and will have to go abroad on loan for the season but Jérémy Jacquet, who has yet to feature, was due to have a fitness test this morning and would be a welcome to boost to a squad whose defence still requires significant reinforcements.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Martin Odegaard may feel aggrieved, but giving Arsenal a foul to disallow Newcastle United's first goal would have been very harsh.

That is according to former PGMOL chief and ex-FIFA referee, Keith Hackett, who exclusively told Football Insider that Chris Kavanagh should have blown immediately if he was going to award the free-kick.

The Magpies claimed a point in a thrilling 2-2 draw against Mikel Arteta's side at St James' Park on Saturday, 21 November.

Eberechi Eze took the lead, but after efforts from Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw, Noni Madueke's goal was needed for the Gunners to avoid defeat.

There was a huge debate over whether Newcastle's equaliser should have stood to begin with, as Joe Willock left Odegaard in a heap on the floor.

Play was allowed to continue, with Barnes scoring as a direct result of the Arsenal being dispossessed, but it was never called back for a foul.

Speaking exclusively to Football Insider, Hackett has disagreed with Arsenal fans asking for a foul, more than happy to go with the referee's decision.

"If you're going to give the free-kick, you're going to have to blow immediately before the ball's hit the back of the net," he mentioned.

"It's hit the back of the net too late. You're not going to give it. That refereeing. And therefore, in that situation, let's go with the referee's call again.

It has been revealed that "Support the referee. It's easy to give these free kicks. Odegaard could feel slightly aggrieved, but I've seen much worse not penalised either.

"Horrendous error!" Harvey Barnes puts Newcastle level 👊 pic.twitter.com/YWrHZPxBIo.

Sources indicate that "So for me, I think I'm not going to rule the goal out. He's the type of player that chases the referee, isn't he? If he thinks something's wrong, he's usually on the doorstep of the referee having a go.".

With Pierre Sage and Michael Carrick gone, the bookies believe that Matthias Jaissle could be one of the next managers sacked this season.

His future at St James' Park has already become a major talking point, and understandably so, given how far the club have fallen in such a short amount of time.

A 2-2 draw against the current Premier League leaders should buy him more than enough time to turn things around, though.

The Magpies are sitting 13th in the table, so clearly, improvements need to be made, but there should be no complications if the performance can be recreated.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox have come under fire already this season, but the club's continued struggles have ramped up the pressure.
  • Berrada in particular has been slammed after his recent interview where he insisted the Red Devils are heading in the right direction and the squad is strong enough to compete.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United fans are becoming increasingly annoyed with the way the club is being run by the current decision-makers.

Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox have come under fire already this season, but the club's continued struggles have ramped up the pressure.

Berrada in particular has been slammed after his recent interview where he insisted the Red Devils are heading in the right direction and the squad is strong enough to compete.

Former Man United chief scout Mick Brown told Football Insider that the fans are not stupid and will see through the blatant attempts by the board to cover up their mistakes.

The decision to sack Michael Carrick and bring in Mauricio Pochettino felt inevitable, but while the fans are ready to get behind their latest manager, they remain angry at the board.

Ongoing concerns about recruitment and the managerial situation have grown, while off-field problems including the treatment of fans will also not be ignored.

Football Insider revealed last month that Man United are fearing a potential dressing room mutiny after both Lisandro Martinez and Bruno Fernandes spoke out.

The fans at Old Trafford are not the only ones who are unhappy with the board's decisions, with the players also growing frustrated, in what is a bad sign for the hierarchy.

While they continue to insist that there are no major problems and things will sort themselves out, the fans can see differently, and are now turning on the decision-makers.

"I still can't think of a single decision this board has made that has had a positive impact," Brown told Football Insider.

"Every now and then, one of them comes out with another statement where they try to pretend everything in the garden is rosy and that there are no major problems.

"Now it's Berrada, trying to convince everybody that they're heading in the right direction and that the squad is good enough, but the Man United fans are not stupid.

"They're not just going to listen to every word he states and think 'well that must be true', because they can see what's happening on the pitch.

"If he genuinely thinks this squad, and the players they've brought in, are good enough to compete, then I have to question how he is still in that job.

"The Man United fans are not happy, the players are not happy, and before long those frustrations are going to be made clear, and it's the likes of Berrada and Wilcox who will face the brunt of it.

"They cannot continue to get away with decisions which are making Man United worse on and off the pitch, because people aren't going to sit by and let it happen.

"The way things have been handled is a disgrace, everybody can see that, but they'll continue to turn a blind eye to it, pretend everything is okay, and hope people will believe them.".

Man United's decision to replace Carrick with Pochettino was made in an attempt to arrest their dismal start to the season and kickstart a turnaround in their form.

However, after a 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in the newly introduced boss' first game, it has become clear that it will take more than a change in manager to resolve the Red Devils' issues.

Brown told Football Insider on 16 November that Pochettino is destined to fail to Man United and has already been hamstrung by the "incompetent" board.

There is a feeling that, regardless of which manager is brought in to steer the ship, they will face an uphill struggle to turn things around with the way the club has been run.

This comes after Pochettino became the fourth permanent manager to take charge at Man United in just four years, with each having suffered from the same problems.

Nottingham Forest have doubts about Oliver Glasner's tactical setup and whether he is getting the best out of his players.

Forest are currently 17th in the Premier League table, only outside of the relegation zone on goal-difference, and have struggled to look convincing so far this season.

A 3-1 win against Man City before the international break looked likely to buy the boss some time, but after a 2-0 defeat to Bournemouth, doubts have grown again.

Former Man United chief scout Mick Brown told Football Insider that Glasner will be under pressure at Nottingham Forest until he can put a run of positive results together.

In the meantime, he remains very much at risk, with Evangelos Marinakis believed to have expected more from the Europa League, FA Cup and Conference League-winning manager.

The controversial owner is notoriously trigger-happy, and if Forest get sucked into a relegation battle, Glasner may not be trusted to get them out of it.

Football Insider revealed on 20 November that.

Following the defeat against Bournemouth, questions are now being asked about the manager's system, and whether it is negatively impacting his players' performances.

At Crystal Palace, Glasner had plenty of success with his 3-4-3 shape, but that has not been the case at Forest and his reluctance to change could pile pressure on his position.

"We've spoken quite a lot about Oliver Glasner already this season, and that's never good," Brown told Football Insider.

"He's always going to be under pressure at Nottingham Forest when results aren't going to initiative, because we know how Evagelos Marinakis likes to opperate.

"That win against Man City will have eased the pressure a bit, but really he needed to build on that win, and instead they went back to their old form against Bournemouth.

"I think one thing that is becoming a problem is that he's not getting the best out of his players with the way he's setting the team up.

"Sometimes as a manager, you have to adapt to suit the players you've got available, whether that's with your formation or with the way you approach games.

"I'm not sure Glasner has been especially willing to do that, and that's led to some lingering doubts, because the way they're playing at the moment isn't getting results.

"If they keep losing games, they're going to be dragged into a relegation battle, and then he could be in trouble.".

Nottingham Forest's board are not the only ones who have grown frustrated with recent performances, as large sections of the fanbase are also having doubts.

Glasner's refusal to adapt and inability to get the best out of his players has raised red flags, while their lack of goalscoring threat has also led to concerns at the City Ground.

The boss was appointed to replace Vitor Pereira in a controversial move, and while it was viewed as a positive change at the time, results this season have not gone to initiative.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 10:30 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 11:25 EST, 20 November 2026.

For anyone with anything resembling a retentive memory, the alarm bells were going off all over the shop on the day Sebastien Pocognoli was unveiled as the new Scotland head coach.

Scottish Football Association (SFA) chief executive Ian Maxwell and chief football officer Craig Mulholland were there to crow about an extensive search of foreign fields to rival Captain Cook’s journeys around the Pacific and how data had helped land ‘one of Europe’s most sought-after coaches’ and secure the ‘aggressive, front-foot style of play’ that was going to bring a desired freshness.

Sources indicate that it was impossible to avoid the elephant in the room, though. Two-and-a-half months earlier, ahead of the disaster zone that was the World Cup, they’d handed Steve Clarke a fresh four-year contract.

He was the polar opposite to Poco. Aggressive and front-foot, he most certainly wasn’t. The SFA knew Clarke didn’t have it in him to go for it at a major finals – as evidenced by two separate European Championship failures – but they decided to stick with the status quo anyway. Just as they did after Euro 2024, when he should have been sacked.

When Clarke finally did go of his own accord after the summer’s events in North America, Maxwell stated he was ‘sad’ the former Kilmarnock manager had stepped down and put a substantial dollop of blame on ‘some fairly hysterical commentary back home’.

SFA chief football officer Craig Mulholland,  Pocognoli and SFA chief executive Ian Maxwell.

Industry observers note that it just didn’t add up. How do you go from thinking a guy like Clarke is the future to tearing everything up, drafting in a London-based analytics firm to tell you who to go for as his replacement and coming up with a 39-year-old Belgian who wants to go for broke?

According to recent reports, ‘It doesn’t matter how you get there,’ offered Maxwell. ‘Let’s not get too hung up on the whys and the what-ifs.’.

Unfortunately, people are now starting to get hung up over the fact Pocognoli, for all the good on his CV, looks like he’s in the wrong movie – with his refusal to break from a failing three-at-the-back strategy suggesting a diploma from the Wilfried Nancy School of Intransigence ought to be on that resume too.

They are getting hung up on the fact captain Andy Robertson came out after the thrashing from Switzerland’s B-team to reveal the mood inside the camp has changed and warn there’s no breathing space to sort this out.

And they are getting hung up on the fact that it’s becoming considerably easier to reach the conclusion those above all of them at the very top of the SFA have never had a proper grip on things at all.

Clarke, of course, only exacerbated those concerns in September by expressing the view at a public event that Maxwell and Co ‘panicked a little bit’ in giving him that incomprehensible long-term deal because he’d threatened to announce he was quitting before the finals unless an agreement was reached.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I wanted to control my narrative,’ he explained. It was hard to know who emerged from those admissions looking worse.

Clarke’s off the plot now, though, and it’s Maxwell, Mulholland and the SFA president Mike Mulraney left to try and convince us all that there is some kind of rhyme or reason to it all.

Sources indicate that how things shape up with Pocognoli is an acid test for them. The rise or fall of a Scotland manager always hogs headlines. Yet, it is only one of a number of things coming together in what is starting to feel like a bit of a perfect storm.

Not so long ago, Maxwell and Mulholland were also yakking plenty about their statement project to increase game time for Scotland-eligible Under-21s.

Industry observers note that it’s already in tatters, by the looks of things. The plans were watered down last month, without anything like the same fanfare, to involve Under-23 players and the intended votes on the proposals were pushed back.

In a recent development, A number of Premiership sides haven’t warmed to it and it remains to be seen whether it goes to a vote at all. Certainly, the radical change the top brass envisioned isn’t going to happen and that can only be regarded as an indicator that these guys running the game aren’t capable of taking it with them.

The start of Sebastien Pocognoli's reign has been concerning for Scotland fans.

Industry observers note that dundee manager Steven Pressley’s intervention over recent days hasn’t helped them either. After a long period on the outside looking in, Scotland have turned out in three major tournaments in the last five years.

Sources indicate that that has raised many millions of pounds, but the effect on elite level is questionable. Pressley talked of the sport being ‘built on sand’ as a result of there being no kind of national facility and you’d better believe it gained traction.

‘It says a lot about our strategy, our longevity and our long-term vision and we are finally seeing the effects of that. We have shown none of that over the period and it is all horribly catching up with us,’ he stated.

In a recent development, the SFA do own Hampden, of course, thanks to that peculiar £5million deal from 2019 that involved Willie Haughey and Sir Tom Hunter ponying up half the money. Yet, how distant those days of Maxwell talking about taking examples from the way VfB Stuttgart revamped the Mercedes-Benz Arena and potentially implementing them in Mount Florida seem now.

Everyone appears to have given up on making the National Stadium better. Other problems have overtaken that old chestnut. Refereeing isn’t good enough. VAR isn’t up to scratch. General facilities require considerable improvement.

Should this Youth Initiative fail, there may also be a need for the SFA to look deeper within when addressing the dearth of top-tier talent coming through.

In a recent development, it’s OK to blame clubs, but what about the level of coaching – and coach education – that exists at the national association? That’s before we even get to the ‘massive lack of expertise and education’ at the younger end of grassroots raised by St Mirren boss Craig McLeish.

In a recent development, the SFA set-up for producing coaches was once the envy of many. We all remember Jose Mourinho and others at the Largs finishing school. Now? Even Maxwell, after stating there were no viable Scottish rivals to Pocognoli for the Scotland job, admitted the coaching pathway needs looked at.

Sources indicate that there is only one problem here, though. Maxwell has been the chief executive since May 2018. He’s in his ninth year in the role. What has he really achieved? What have his major ideas been?

Industry observers note that yes, Scotland made it back to major finals under Clarke, but Clarke was a painfully obvious choice to be made national coach in 2019. He’d worked wonders at Rugby Park and did transfer that to the international scene until it came to actually turning out in those showpiece competitions.

Now they’ve had to get creative, there is so much hanging on Pocognoli’s reign for the guys at the top.

Maxwell was a bloke who landed in the role of Partick Thistle GM almost by mistake after failing to beat Jackie McNamara to the manager’s job. Just before leaving for the SFA, the Jags got relegated.

Talk of redeveloping Hampden has gone quiet as other problems take the spotlight.

At his Hampden unveiling, he had to fend off questions about only getting that position through behind-the-scenes politicking and insist he wouldn’t be a puppet for anyone.

Mulholland also seems a surprising choice as the architect of the national sport’s renovation. He spent two decades in the Rangers academy and eight years as head of it.

Recent findings suggest that has it been a conveyor belt of talent for the Ibrox first-team? Do you recall much wailing and gnashing of teeth when he left in 2023 amid a wider changing of the guard?

Then, there’s Mulraney, the former Alloa chairman and SFA director for over a decade.

Sources indicate that you don’t see much of him these days. Maybe because people want to ask about his position as chair of FIFA’s finance committee in the wake of the most greed-infested World Cup ever and the ongoing soap opera surrounding Gianni Infantino. But maybe not.

How things work out with Pocognoli might end up being the one thing that puts all these guys under the kind of examination that cannot be bodyswerved, but it’s only the tip of the iceberg.

By Saikat Mandal | 22 Nov 2026 18:54, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 19:40.

Liverpool produced arguably their finest performance under Andoni Iraola as they thrashed Manchester United 4-0 in Sunday's Premier League clash at Anfield.

The victory keeps the Reds third in the Premier League table, but they have closed the gap on Manchester City to one point and remain seven points adrift of leaders Arsenal.

Just eight minutes into Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge, the Red Devils were reduced to 10 men after Leny Yoro was shown a straight red card for a challenge on Alexander Isak.

From the resulting free kick, Dominik Szoboszlai fired Liverpool into the lead, before the hosts strengthened their advantage when Florian Wirtz finished off a brilliant move down the flank involving Rio Ngumoha.

The Reds youngster got on the scoresheet himself in the second half, while substitute Victor Munoz put the finishing touches on a commanding display by netting the fourth goal.

With Cody Gakpo unavailable, Iraola handed Ngumoha a place in the starting lineup, and the youngster delivered an electrifying performance on the night.

According to Opta Joe, Ngumoha became the youngest player ever to register a goal involvement in a Premier League match between Liverpool and Manchester United.

Picking up possession, he bamboozled his marker before whipping in a superb left-footed cross, which Wirtz emphatically converted to put Liverpool 2-0 ahead.

After the break, Bradley Barcola escaped his marker and played a perfectly weighted pass into Ngumoha's path, leaving the youngster with a simple finish.

In doing so, Ngumoha also became the youngest player to score and provide an assist in a Premier League match since Michael Owen achieved the feat on Boxing Day 1997.

Reports have emerged in recent weeks suggesting that Bayern Munich remain interested in signing Ngumoha, but Liverpool should not entertain any offers for the highly-rated youngster.

Ngumoha is already receiving more opportunities under Iraola and is expected to play a significant role this season.

Liverpool rate him highly, and there is little doubt that he could develop into a regular first-team fixture as he continues to mature.

While Yoro's dismissal certainly helped Liverpool take control of the contest, Man Utd offered little to trouble the hosts and failed to frustrate them by remaining resolute at the back.
