📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Savio's injury has left Tottenham Hotspur boss Roberto De Zerbi furious with the decision to let him play.

That is the opinion of former senior Tottenham scout, Bryan King, speaking exclusively to Football Insider.

The 22-year-old wide forward made his return from injury during Saturday's 2-0 win over Ipswich Town, having spent more than a month out with a muscle injury.

But after just 25 minutes on the pitch, Savio pulled up and was forced to limp off the pitch, with De Zerbi confirming after the game that he has suffered the same injury.

Tottenham agreed a deal worth up to £85million to sign the Brazilian from Manchester City in the summer, but have had just seven appearances out of him so far this season.

The emergence of Luca Williams-Barnett may hand the forward another problem on his eventual return, with the youngster impressing in his position.

“IT’S THE SAME INJURY!” 😤 Roberto De Zerbi on Sávio’s injury setback on his return against Ipswich pic.twitter.com/VfJzxuZ2Gy.

Injuries have been a constant problem for Tottenham this season, but none have been more frustrating than Savio's.

The winger has looked exciting whenever he has been on the pitch, but the Lilywhites have struggled to keep him on it.

"Those types of injuries are very risky, you've got to be very sure [that they are ready to return]," King told Football Insider.

"I could imagine the physio would have said to the player, 'look do you want to give it another week or another two weeks?' 'No, I feel fine'.

In a recent development, "Well, now you've got to make your decision - are you fine or are you not? Do you feel confident about going to play in the Premier League? If you make that decision, it's on your head then.

"I think the thing that De Zerbi is angry about is that he obviously wasn't ready, because he came on before the 70th minute and he went off about 25 minutes later.

In a recent development, "Injuries are very, very risky. You come back too early and, if you've been out five weeks, you're obviously desperate to come back. You want to get back in the team like he obviously did, and it's backfired on him and the club because he could be out now for another five weeks.

"I understand De Zerbi being angry because that's down to the physio and the player himself.".

Savio's injury left a bad taste after what had been a really positive day for Tottenham.

The Lilywhites had won their fourth Premier League game from five and are now just one point behind Chelsea.

After the game, a clearly frustrated De Zerbi mentioned: "Yes I'm very angry about that because Savio is a crucial player for us.

Industry observers note that "He is there to make the difference for us. It's the same injury and it's the worst thing from today.".

By Saikat Mandal | 22 Nov 2026 19:24.

Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United reign got off to a disastrous start as the Red Devils suffered a humiliating 4-0 defeat against arch-rivals Liverpool at Anfield in the Premier League on Sunday.

The Argentine took charge of the club earlier this week after Man Utd parted ways with Michael Carrick, leaving him with barely a few days to work with his upcoming players on the training ground.

Pochettino had won just three of his previous 19 games before Sunday's encounter, and the final whistle brought no improvement to that record.

The defeat also had a damaging impact on the league standings, with Man Utd dropping to 19th in the Premier League table on eight points after 11 matches, with only Crystal Palace faring worse.

According to Opta Joe, Pochettino became the first manager in Premier League history to see his team concede twice and receive a red card in the first half of his opening match in charge of a club.

The game was only eight minutes old when the Man Utd backline was caught napping, forcing Leny Yoro into a challenge on Alexander Isak that resulted in a red card.

Liverpool capitalised on United's defensive frailties, scoring twice before the break through Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz.

The hosts enjoyed greater control after the interval and added two more goals through Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz, with the former also setting a Premier League record of his own.

Pochettino also entered the Man Utd history books for the wrong reasons, suffering the joint-heaviest defeat by any Red Devils manager in his first game in charge, matching Lal Hilditch's 4-0 loss against Bolton Wanderers in October 1926.

Considering Man Utd's struggles so far this season, the defeat against Liverpool need not spell the end of the world for the Red Devils or their latest manager.

Pochettino's immediate priority will be to collect as many points as possible and create some breathing space between his side and the teams at the bottom of the table.

There were precious few positives to take from the performance, aside from Senne Lammens's display, but Pochettino will hope to see greater improvement from his players in the coming days.

By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 10:25 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 11:32 EST, 20 November 2026.

Manchester United CEO Omar Berrada insists the team got 'fundamentally better' after this summer's transfer window, as he warned ‘spending just for the sake of it’ is not the route to putting United back on top.

In his first sit-down interview in five months, Berrada tackled topics ranging from the relationship between the Glazers and Ineos, the imminent departure of youngster JJ Gabriel, the decision not to sign a left back in the summer, as well as the decision to push ahead for a fresh stadium despite supporter backlash on matchdays.

The United chief has been at the centre of furious protests and anti-ownership chanting at matches this season, alongside Director of Football Jason Wilcox, and he accepted that criticism of United's leadership has, mostly, been fair.

In an interview that aired shortly after new head coach Mauricio Pochettino spoke to the media for the first time, Berrada was pressed on how much accountability falls at his door with United heading to Anfield this weekend 18th in the Premier League table.

'I think if you think about the fact we've had three permanent managers in less than three seasons, clearly we haven't achieved the stability that we wanted, that's for sure,' Berrada told Sky Sports.

According to recent reports, 'When it doesn't work out with the coach or the manager, we are all responsible. Myself, the football leadership, everyone who is involved around the coach and the staff and the players. We have to continue improving and getting better.

Manchester United's CEO Omar Berrada finally fronted up in an interview with Sky Sports.

Michael Carrick's sacking was yet another managerial change at United, with the hierarchy under massive scrutiny and Mauricio Pochettino now in the hotseat.

'There are different circumstances why it didn't work out with Erik [ten Hag], and Ruben [Amorim], and now Michael [Carrick], and we are always learning and, as I said, trying to improve and understand what has failed.

'The challenge is we're trying to find the right manager for the squad that we have with a specific set of skills in that moment to make them perform at their best level.

'It's true, we have to accept the criticism that we haven't been able to achieve that stability with one coach and our aim is to do that as soon as possible. Of course, we hope now that Mauricio coming in will give us that stability that I think we all need.'.

Berrada's links to Manchester City, where he worked prior to joining United, were brought up, not least given he worked at the club during the period that City have had charges brought against them.

'I'm not concerned,' Berrada insisted.

But at his latest home there are problems aplenty, not least having got another managerial appointment wrong, sacking Carrick less than six months after handing him a two-year deal, and so it was put to Berrada: is the club actually progressing?

'It's not good enough, not acceptable and that's why we've made the change that we made so that we can move forward,' he concluded.

(L-R) Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Berrada and Jason Wilcox have drawn plenty of ire from Man United fans.

It has been revealed that 'But we are laying the foundations for sustained growth, to put us in a position where we can be competitive consistently. It's not always been that.

'Last year we finished third, we were happy with the squad, we were happy with the way we were going. And now, a few months later, we are not where we need to be. But the foundations are there and I am convinced that we are heading in the right direction. Very positive.'.
